news.Title: Marvell-Lumentum Deal Reportedly Would Carry Limited Premium
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Semiconductor and data-infrastructure business Marvell Technology Inc. ( MRVL , Financials ) is said to be looking at an all-stock purchase of optical-networking provider Lumentum that would not provide shareholders a substantial premium.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with MRVL.

Is MRVL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The new story added substance to prior signs the businesses were in advanced negotiations on an acquisition.

Shares of Lumentum declined roughly 3.9% after the report, implying that investors were counting on a higher price for the purchase.

Marvell shares also came under pressure, trading down around 8.7%.

An all-stock arrangement might decrease Marvell's immediate financial requirements, but it also would dilute current owners depending on the eventual exchange ratio.

For Marvell, Lumentum would extend its reach into optical components for high-speed networking and AI data centers, a market with growing demand for faster links between GPUs and servers.

Valuation and dilution will dictate how investors see the purchase, but the strategic reasoning may be compelling.

No final transaction value, exchange ratio or verified announcement date was disclosed by the source.

Now the next trigger will be corporations publicly announcing a deal and the premium and financing parameters.

news.Title: Marvell may buy its own laser supplier as investors pull back
news.Content:
Every video call you join and every chatbot answer you get travels part of its trip as laser light. Marvell Technology (MRVL) makes chips that work alongside many of those lasers.

Lumentum Holdings (LITE) makes many of the lasers, and it can't keep up. CEO Michael Hurlston said this month its optical parts are sold out through early 2029, Bloomberg reported .

Marvell may have found a permanent fix. The chipmaker, which already buys lasers from Lumentum, is in advanced talks to buy the company, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. A deal could come as soon as next week, though nothing is signed.

Marvell's investors pulled back hard. The stock fell about 13% on Thursday, October 29, 2026.

The problem is size. Lumentum was worth about $83 billion before the report. Marvell held about $3.9 billion in cash at the end of its latest quarter, according to its earnings release .

Also read: Bank of America tweaks Marvell stock target after key Analyst Day

Bloomberg reported that Marvell would likely pay in shares. I understand why Marvell wants to own its bottleneck. I'm far less comfortable with the currency.

Marvell's shareholders started paying on Thursday

An all-stock deal moves the risk onto Marvell's share price. Lumentum holders would be paid in Marvell stock, so every drop in its share price shrinks the offer.

Marvell's market value ended Thursday near $191 billion . Bloomberg had valued it at about $221 billion before the report. The one-session loss comes to roughly $29 billion .

That loss alone equals more than a third of Lumentum's entire value. To me, Marvell's owners took a takeover-sized hit without seeing a single term.

Lumentum's stock told the same story. Its shares rose as much as 7% on Thursday. By the close, the gain had shrunk to less than 1%.

I read that fade as the market marking down the premium in real time. When the buyer pays in stock, a falling stock means a smaller prize.

Owning a supplier could cost Marvell some customers

The deeper risk may not be the price. In 2023, Lumentum bought Cloud Light, a maker of optical transceiver modules, for about $750 million, according to a company filing .

Rival module makers buy Marvell's signal-processing chips. After a deal, Marvell would own a competitor to some of its own customers.

Stifel estimated that Marvell holds 60% to 65% of the market for one key type of those chips, according to Seeking Alpha . The firm warned that a merger could cost Marvell share if rival module makers switch suppliers.

RBC Capital Markets still said a combination "makes strategic sense given the highly complementary product portfolios," according to Seeking Alpha. It also noted that Marvell outsources its chipmaking, while Lumentum runs its own laser fabs. Combining the two could make margins swing more, RBC warned.

Story Continues

Stifel said the closing would likely take time and require approval from both U.S. and Chinese regulators, according to Investing.com . It also listed building a scaled-up U.S. transceiver supplier, given possible limits on Chinese modules, as one of the deal's drivers.

A deal built partly around limits on Chinese modules may still need Beijing's sign-off. That irony is what I'd watch most closely.

More Artificial Intelligence:

AI's biggest business opportunity may not look like AI

AI racks are outgrowing old power: 2 chipmakers have a strategy

BofA splits software into winners and losers as AI agents arrive

What the deal could mean for both stocks

Marvell entered the week as a big 2026 winner. The stock set an intraday all-time high of $329.88 in June. Its 52-week low of $70.69 shows how fast that run came.

The 47 analysts at StockAnalysis rate Marvell a Strong Buy . Their average target of $340.56 sits far above Thursday's close. Piper Sandler and Stifel kept Buy ratings that day.

Lumentum's climb has been even steeper. Its all-time low was about $14 in October 2015. Its intraday record of $1,143 came on October 9, 2026.

The 28 analysts at StockAnalysis rate Lumentum a Buy . Their average target of $1,166 was last updated before the deal talks, so it reflects the business, not a buyout.

Thursday's nearly flat close suggests the market isn't counting on a rich Lumentum premium. Three things will settle it:

The exchange ratio will show how much of the combined company Lumentum holders would own.

Lumentum's quarterly results are expected Thursday, November 5, 2026, according to a press release .

Plans for Cloud Light will show whether Marvell intends to compete with its chip customers.

If I owned Marvell, I wouldn't sell into Thursday's drop, but I wouldn't add until the terms are public. For Lumentum, I'd wait for the November 5 report before buying.

Scarce lasers could change how chipmakers shop

When a part gets this scarce, buyers stop haggling over supply and start buying the supplier. Stifel listed securing laser supply among this deal's drivers.

With Lumentum sold out into 2029, chip designers that need lasers are negotiating from a position of weakness. If Marvell signs, I expect investors to view every independent laser maker as a supplier a chip giant can't do without.

news.Title: Should You Buy, Sell, or Hold ALAB Stock Before Q3 Earnings Release?
news.Content:
Astera Labs ALAB is set to report its third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 3.

For the third quarter of 2026, revenues are expected to be between $540 million and $560 million. The midpoint implies sequential growth of approximately 40%. Management projects non-GAAP earnings between $1.16 and $1.21 per share.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter 2026 revenues is currently pegged at $550.39 million, indicating an increase of 138.71% from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

The consensus mark for earnings is currently pegged at $1.19 per share, which has been unchanged over the past 30 days. This implies 142.86% year-over-year growth.

Astera Labs, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Astera Labs, Inc. price-eps-surprise | Astera Labs, Inc. Quote

ALAB's earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate in each of the trailing four quarters, with an average earnings surprise of 17.07%.

Let's see how things have shaped up prior to this announcement.

Factors to Note for ALAB's Q3 Earnings

Astera Labs is expected to have benefited from accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, growing demand for high-speed connectivity solutions and increasing adoption of its Scorpio AI Fabric Switches in the third quarter of fiscal 2026. Expanding hyperscaler investments in AI training and inference infrastructure, coupled with increasing accelerator cluster sizes and bandwidth requirements, are likely to have supported demand for the company's intelligent connectivity portfolio.

The transition of Scorpio X-Series high-radix AI Fabric Switches into volume production is expected to have been a major growth catalyst in the to-be-reported quarter. Strong demand from a leading hyperscaler customer, particularly for its 320-lane switching solutions, is likely to have accelerated revenue growth. Scorpio is expected to become Astera Labs' largest product family by revenues in the third quarter, surpassing Aries. Growing adoption of Scorpio P-Series across AI networking, storage and scale-out applications is likely to have contributed to top-line expansion.

The Aries signal conditioning portfolio is expected to have benefited from accelerating adoption of PCIe 6 retimers and gearboxes across AI servers, GPUs and general-purpose computing platforms. Increasing AI accelerator cluster sizes, higher retimer attach rates, and improved average selling prices associated with PCIe 6 adoption are likely to have strengthened Aries revenues. Continued demand for PCIe 5 solutions across inference applications is also expected to have supported growth.

The Taurus portfolio is likely to have benefited from increasing demand for high-speed Ethernet connectivity across AI and general-purpose computing platforms. Strong adoption of 400G solutions, alongside initial preproduction shipments of 100-gigabit-per-lane Taurus Smart Cable Modules supporting 800G Ethernet connectivity, is expected to have boosted revenues. Expanding 800G deployments are likely to have supported improved attach rates and higher average selling prices.

However, Astera Labs' third-quarter 2026 performance is likely to have faced pressure from declining gross margins due to an evolving product mix and rising operating expenses associated with continued investments in product development.

Story Continues

ALAB Shares Outperform Sector, Industry

Astera Labs shares have risen 74.6% in the year-to-date period, outperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's return of 14.2% and the Zacks Internet Software industry's rise of 0.2%.

ALAB Stock Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Astera Labs stock is not so cheap, as the Value Score of F suggests a stretched valuation at this moment.

In terms of the forward 12-month Price/Sales, ALAB is trading at 17.79X, higher than the Zacks Internet Software industry's 3.98X.

ALAB Valuation

ALAB Faces Stiff Competition

Despite an expanding portfolio and strong partner base, ALAB is facing stiff competition from other industry players like Marvell Technology MRVL, Credo Technology CRDO and Cisco Systems CSCO. These companies are all expanding their footprints in the AI infrastructure space.

Marvell Technology has expanded its AI connectivity portfolio with the introduction of the Alaska E 3.2T protocol-aware retimer and second-generation Alaska A 1.6T active electrical cable DSP. Built on advanced 3nm technology, these solutions address growing bandwidth, latency and power-efficiency requirements in AI infrastructure. The Alaska E delivers 3.2 Tbps bandwidth across 16 lanes, supporting Ethernet, UALink and ESUN protocols. The Alaska A offers 1.6T throughput, more than six meters of copper reach and improved power efficiency. Both products are currently sampling to customers, strengthening Marvell Technology's position in next-generation AI scale-up networking.

Credo Technology's expanding portfolio has been noteworthy. In August 2026, the company announced that it is developing a new open interconnect standard within the Open Compute Project (OCP). It has established the OCP Open Chiplet Economy Lightweight Serial Interconnect (LSI) Workstream, aimed at developing efficient interconnect solutions for AI infrastructure. As part of the initiative, Credo Technology plans to contribute its OmniConnect lightweight AXI framer specification to OCP. The OCP LSI initiative is designed to support an open, interoperable ecosystem where compute, memory and other resources can be combined more efficiently. This could allow data-center operators and AI developers to tailor systems to specific workloads rather than relying on fixed architectures.

Cisco's AI infrastructure business continues to gain momentum. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the company secured $4 billion in hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders, bringing fiscal 2026 orders to $9.3 billion, approximately 4.5 times the previous year's level. The company's Silicon One architecture, particularly its P200 and G200-powered systems and Acacia optical solutions, is strengthening its competitive position. Cisco expects hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenues to reach $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027 compared with approximately $4 billion in fiscal 2026.

Conclusion

Astera Labs' expanding AI connectivity portfolio and accelerating Scorpio adoption are likely to drive strong third-quarter growth. However, stretched valuation, intensifying competition and margin pressures remain risks.

Astera Labs currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), suggesting that it may be wise to wait for a more favorable entry point to accumulate the stock. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: MRVL vs. SNDK: Which AI Infrastructure Stock is a Safer Bet?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology MRVL and Sandisk SNDK are benefiting from the expanding artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure market, but their businesses address different requirements. Marvell develops custom silicon, networking and connectivity solutions that help AI systems process and transmit data. Sandisk supplies NAND flash-based storage products, including enterprise solid-state drives (SSDs), that support data-intensive workloads.

As AI infrastructure spending expands, both companies have opportunities to grow revenues and earnings. However, differences in growth visibility, profitability, valuation and execution risks raise the question: Which stock is the better investment right now?

The Case for MRVL Stock

Marvell is benefiting from rising demand for custom AI silicon, high-speed optical interconnects and advanced networking solutions. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, revenues increased 36.5% year over year to $2.74 billion, while non-GAAP earnings rose 40.3% to 94 cents per share. Data center revenues reached a record $2.17 billion, up 46% year over year, accounting for 79% of total revenues.

The company is expanding its AI infrastructure portfolio as hyperscalers invest in larger and more complex AI clusters. Demand for 800G optical digital signal processors remains strong, while 1.6T products are ramping rapidly. Marvell also expects its scale-out switching business to more than double in fiscal 2027, supported by wider adoption of its 51.2T products.

Custom silicon represents another important growth opportunity. Management expects the business to more than double year over year in fiscal 2028, with further acceleration anticipated in fiscal 2029. Marvell's expanded commercial agreement with a key hyperscaler covers existing and potential programs involving AI accelerators, storage controllers, network interface cards and memory interface controllers.

Strategic ties with NVIDIA and the acquisitions of Celestial AI and XConn Technologies further expand Marvell's opportunities in optical interconnects and next-generation AI networking. Management expects fiscal 2027 revenues to increase approximately 45% to $12 billion and fiscal 2028 revenues to reach roughly $18 billion, implying growth of about 50% in the latter year.

Nevertheless, Marvell faces margin pressure as custom silicon scales, along with customer concentration, supply constraints, geopolitical exposure and uneven communications demand. Its growing dependence on data center customers makes execution and hyperscaler spending particularly important. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MRVL's fiscal 2027 earnings suggests year-over-year growth of 48%. Estimates have remained unchanged in the past 30 days.

Story Continues

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Case for SNDK Stock

Sandisk is benefiting from accelerating demand for enterprise storage as AI workloads require greater capacity and performance. The company's first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues surged 378% year over year and increased 23% sequentially to $11.03 billion. SNDK's data center revenues increased 61% sequentially to $4.80 billion, reflecting strong demand for enterprise SSDs across hyperscalers and AI infrastructure customers.

The company reported significant growth in its TLC enterprise SSD business and continued ramping of its QLC products, which address capacity-intensive applications such as AI data lakes, vector databases and retrieval repositories. SNDK's edge revenues rose 7% sequentially to $5.83 billion, supported by resilience in premium and mainstream markets and stronger automotive and IoT demand.

Sandisk's technology roadmap, including BiCS8, BiCS9 and BiCS10, supports higher storage density, interface performance and bandwidth. BiCS9 is expected to improve interface performance through next-generation CMOS, while BiCS10 introduces a 1-terabit TLC die for performance-intensive workloads and a 2-terabit QLC die with twice the read and write bandwidth of BiCS8. Its high-bandwidth flash (HBF) technology also advanced during the quarter, with the first HBF memory die completing tape-out and fabrication underway.

Sandisk expects to deliver samples of its first HBF-based products in 2027, although this opportunity is not yet included in its long-term financial model. SNDK's profitability and cash generation remain strong. Sandisk's non-GAAP gross margin increased to 85.1% from 84.6% in the preceding quarter, while non-GAAP operating margin improved to 80.4% from 79.2%. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for SNDK's fiscal 2027 earnings suggests year-over-year growth of 200%. Estimates have been revised upward in the past seven days.

Stock Price Performance and Valuation of MRVL & SNDK

In the year-to-date period, MRVL shares have gained 157% compared with the surge of 460.4% in SNDK shares.

YTD Performance Chart

SNDK is trading at a forward sales multiple of 3.29X, way below its median of 4.11X. MRVL's forward sales multiple sits at 9.90X, higher than its median of 9.44X over the past year.

Forward 12-Month (P/S) Valuation Chart

Conclusion: MRVL vs. SNDK

Sandisk appears better positioned than Marvell at present, supported by significantly stronger revenue growth, expanding profitability and a more attractive valuation. While Marvell offers promising opportunities in custom AI silicon, optical interconnects and networking, Sandisk is benefiting from the growing importance of NAND storage in AI infrastructure, with data center revenues accelerating rapidly. This is strongly supported by SNDK's massive bottom-line growth projection. SNDK and MRVL carry a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) each at present. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Twilio Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Revenue Growth
news.Content:
Twilio Inc. TWLO reported better-than-expected third-quarter 2026 results, with both earnings and revenues surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Non-GAAP earnings of $1.65 per share beat the consensus mark by 13%. The bottom line increased 32% from the year-ago quarter's earnings of $1.25 per share, driven by robust revenue growth and operating leverage.

The cloud-based communications platform provider reported revenues of $1.56 billion, surpassing the consensus estimate by 3.1%. Revenues increased 20% year over year, driven by broad-based product strength and growing AI-related demand. The dollar-based net expansion rate was 114%, up from 109% a year ago.

TWLO's Q3 Revenue Growth Drivers

Twilio's organic revenues increased 16% year over year to $1.50 billion. Organic growth excludes incremental U.S. carrier pass-through fees and acquisition-related revenues. The company benefited from healthy demand across messaging, voice and software add-ons, alongside sustained momentum among AI-native customers.

Messaging revenues grew 24% year over year, supported by higher volumes and increased adoption of WhatsApp and Rich Communication Services. Incremental U.S. carrier fees contributed approximately seven percentage points to messaging revenue growth. Messaging accounted for 59% of total revenues during the quarter.

Twilio Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Twilio Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Twilio Inc. Quote

Voice revenues increased more than 20%, reflecting higher usage volumes and growing adoption of software add-ons. The self-serve channel registered revenue growth exceeding 30%, while independent software vendor revenues advanced more than 20%. Software add-on revenues grew more than 25%, and support and services revenues increased more than 30%.

Twilio's AI Momentum Supports Customer Expansion

Twilio witnessed continued adoption of its AI-enabled communications capabilities, including Conversation Relay, Conversational Intelligence and Branded Calling. Management highlighted growing demand from AI-native businesses deploying voice agents and expanding their usage across multiple communication channels.

The company secured several notable customer agreements during the quarter. Ushur signed a seven-figure expansion involving voice AI capabilities, while Gong renewed a seven-figure agreement. Twilio also secured its first eight-figure Conversations deal with a health insurance provider, underscoring growing enterprise interest in AI-powered customer engagement.

Story Continues

Management noted that voice AI represents approximately 1% of overall voice interactions, highlighting the early stage of adoption. Twilio is also developing identity verification capabilities for AI agents, with an offering currently in private beta and general availability planned for 2027.

TWLO's Profitability Improves Despite Carrier Fees

Non-GAAP gross profit increased 18% year over year to $767.8 million. However, non-GAAP gross margin contracted 90 basis points year over year to 49.2%, primarily due to $53 million of incremental U.S. carrier pass-through fees. Excluding these fees, gross margin would have expanded 80 basis points.

Non-GAAP income from operations surged 39% year over year to $325.7 million. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 290 basis points to approximately 21%, reflecting strong gross profit growth and cost efficiencies. Operating income benefited from approximately $11 million in platform credits.

Twilio's Cash Generation Remains Strong

Net cash provided by operating activities reached $389.2 million compared with $263.6 million in the prior-year quarter. Free cash flow increased approximately 49% year over year to $369.6 million, with a free cash flow margin of 24%, up from 19%.

Twilio ended the third quarter with $1.06 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $1.83 billion in short-term marketable securities. Long-term debt stood at $993.6 million. The company repurchased $127.2 million of shares during the quarter, leaving approximately $700 million under its existing authorization.

TWLO Raises Its 2026 Outlook

For 2026, Twilio raised its reported revenue growth outlook to 20% from 18-18.5% and its organic revenue growth projection to 15% from 13-13.5%. The company also increased its non-GAAP income from operations and free cash flow guidance to $1.19-$1.20 billion each compared with the previous range of $1.135-$1.155 billion.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Twilio expects revenues between $1.595 billion and $1.605 billion, indicating reported growth of 17-17.5% and organic growth of 11-12%. Non-GAAP income from operations is projected at $300-$310 million, with non-GAAP earnings of $1.48-$1.53 per share.

Twilio Provides an Upbeat 2027 Preliminary Outlook

Management expects organic revenue growth of at least 10% in 2027, exceeding its earlier long-term framework of 7-8%. Non-GAAP gross profit growth is anticipated to remain broadly aligned with organic revenue growth.

Twilio also projects non-GAAP income from operations and free cash flow of at least $1.35 billion each in 2027.

Twilio's Zacks Rank & Other Stocks to Consider

Currently, TWLO carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

Some other top-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector are Analog Devices ADI, Autodesk ADSK and Cisco Systems CSCO, each carrying a Zacks Rank #2 at present. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Shares of Analog Devices have rallied 85.3% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ADI's fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $13.00 per share, up by 4 cents over the past 30 days, indicating an increase of 66.9% year over year.

Shares of Autodesk have plunged 19.6% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ADSK's fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $12.62 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days, indicating a rise of 21% year over year.

Cisco Systems shares have surged 50.5% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CSCO's fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $5.11 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days, indicating an increase of 18% year over year.

news.Title: ASE Technology Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on AI-Driven LEAP Growth
news.Content:
ASE Technology Holding ASX reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of 37 cents per ADS, which increased 125.3% year over year and beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 8.8%.

Revenues surged 44.8% year over year and 27.8% sequentially to NT$244.16 billion. In U.S. dollar terms, revenues of $7.64 billion surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.3%. Results reflected robust artificial intelligence (AI)-driven demand for Leading-edge Advanced Packaging (LEAP) services, with Assembly, Testing and Materials (ATM) revenues climbing 51% year over year.

ASX ATM Growth Accelerates on LEAP Demand

ATM revenues totaled NT$151.49 billion, up 20.1% sequentially and 51% year over year. Packaging revenues surged 52.5% to NT$122.95 billion, while testing revenues advanced 42.8% to NT$26.30 billion.

Management cited strong demand across LEAP and conventional semiconductor services, with capacity operating at or near full utilization. Faster-than-expected installations of LEAP capacity supported revenue growth, while demand continued to exceed available supply across advanced and mainstream packaging operations.

ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. Quote

ASE Technology Revenue Mix Shifts Toward Computing

Computing represented 34% of ATM revenues, up from 25% in the year-ago quarter. Communication's contribution declined to 38% from 45%, while automotive, consumer and other applications accounted for 28%.

By service type, bumping, flip-chip, wafer-level packaging and system-in-package services contributed 51% of ATM revenues. Wire bonding accounted for 24%, testing represented 17%, other services contributed 6%, and materials made up 2%.

Management expects computing applications to remain a major growth driver through 2027 and 2028, supported by increasing LEAP adoption in high-performance computing and other advanced semiconductor applications.

ASE Technology's EMS Results Stay Mixed

Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) revenues increased 35.4% year over year and 42.1% sequentially to NT$93.47 billion. Consumer applications represented 41% of EMS revenues, computing contributed 21%, and communication accounted for 19%.

EMS gross margin declined 60 basis points sequentially to 8.3%, reflecting higher pass-through component costs and product-mix changes. However, operating margin improved to 3.3% from 2.4% in the prior quarter, supported by operating expense leverage.

Story Continues

Management noted that growing demand for AI accelerators contributed to computing revenue expansion, while elevated component costs continued to weigh on profitability.

ASE Technology Margins Expand

Consolidated gross profit increased 86.9% year over year to NT$53.97 billion. Gross margin expanded 500 basis points to 22.1%, reflecting stronger ATM revenues, favorable LEAP product mix and currency benefits.

Operating income surged 151% to NT$33.14 billion, while operating margin improved 580 basis points to 13.6%. Operating expenses increased to NT$20.82 billion, mainly due to higher headcount, profit-sharing expenses and research and development spending.

ATM gross margin reached 30.6%, up from 22.6% a year earlier, while operating margin expanded to 20% from 10.8%. Management indicated that increasing LEAP contributions have pushed profitability beyond the segment's previous structural margin ceiling.

ASX Investment Spending Moves Higher

Equipment capital expenditures totaled $2.10 billion during the third quarter, including $991 million for packaging operations, $1.07 billion for testing, $41 million for EMS and $5 million for interconnect materials and other activities.

The company additionally invested approximately $1.8 billion in facilities and land during the quarter. Management raised its 2026 capital expenditure budget to $11.5 billion from $10.5 billion, reflecting continued investment in semiconductor capacity expansion.

ASE Technology has 22 ongoing building projects in Taiwan, with more than half expected to begin supporting revenues by 2027. Management anticipates higher capital expenditures in 2027 as capacity constraints persist.

ASX Balance Sheet Remains Healthy

As of Sept. 30, 2026, ASE Technology held NT$107.94 billion in cash, cash equivalents and current financial assets. Total interest-bearing debt increased to NT$406.46 billion, while unused credit facilities totaled NT$457.28 billion. The net debt-to-equity ratio was 0.66.

Net cash generated from operating activities reached NT$50.46 billion during the quarter.

ASX Outlook Remains Strong

For the fourth quarter of 2026, management expects consolidated revenues to increase 6-8% sequentially in New Taiwan dollar terms. Gross margin is projected between 23% and 24%, while operating margin is expected in the 14.5-15.5% range. ATM revenues are forecast to grow 11-13% sequentially, with gross margin improving 100-200 basis points. EMS revenues are expected to remain relatively flat, with operating margin around 2%.

Management raised its 2026 LEAP revenue outlook to more than $4 billion and expects LEAP revenues to double in 2027. Full-process packaging revenues are projected to exceed $1 billion in 2027, while co-packaged optics revenues are expected to surpass $500 million, supported by sustained demand for advanced semiconductor technologies.

ASX Zacks Rank & Other Stocks to Consider

ASE Technology Holding currently flaunts a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Some other top-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector are Analog Devices ADI, Autodesk ADSK and Cisco Systems CSCO, each carrying a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) at present. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Shares of Analog Devices have rallied 85.3% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ADI's fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $13.00 per share, up by 4 cents over the past 30 days, indicating an increase of 66.9% year over year.

Shares of Autodesk have plunged 19.6% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ADSK's fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $12.62 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days, indicating a rise of 21% year over year.

Cisco Systems shares have surged 50.5% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CSCO's fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $5.11 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days, indicating an increase of 18% year over year.

news.Title: SIMO Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI and Enterprise Growth Outlook
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO outlined an ambitious growth outlook during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, emphasizing expanding opportunities in enterprise storage, automotive applications and AI infrastructure.

Management expects revenue to grow at least 40% in 2027, supported by customer design wins, improving product mix and rising demand for specialized storage solutions, despite persistent weakness in consumer markets.

SIMO Projects Strong Growth Through 2027

Fourth-quarter revenues are expected between $588 million and $616 million, representing sequential growth of 5% to 10%. Non-GAAP gross margin is expected between 54% and 55%, with operating margin reaching 36% to 37%.

For 2027, revenue growth is expected to be at least 40%, with gross margins remaining in the low-to-mid-50% range. Management anticipates continued operating leverage as enterprise and automotive products contribute more revenue.

During the quarter, revenues reached $560 million, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $532.8 million. Adjusted earnings of $4.35 per ADS surpassed the consensus estimate of $3.30.

Silicon Motion Technology Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Silicon Motion Technology Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Silicon Motion Technology Corporation Quote

Silicon Motion Sees Enterprise Storage Momentum

Chief executive officer Wallace Kou emphasized growing demand for MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers across NAND manufacturers, hyperscalers and cloud service providers.

All seven announced MonTitan customers remain on track for commercial production ramps during 2026. The company also completed tape-out of its next-generation 4nm PCIe Gen 6 controller, with sampling scheduled for the first quarter of 2027.

Management expects TLC-based enterprise SSD demand to lead near-term growth, while QLC-based storage opportunities expand as higher-density NAND becomes available. Kou expects broader adoption to strengthen MonTitan's contribution beyond 2026.

SIMO Expands Automotive and Boot Drive Opportunities

Kou highlighted Ferri automotive and enterprise boot drives as major growth engines. Combined solutions revenues increased more than 75% sequentially and represented over 40% of third-quarter sales.

Automotive products benefited from expanding customer relationships and higher margins. Management also identified opportunities in robotics, drones and advanced networking, although robotics demand remains at an early stage.

Enterprise boot drives represent another expansion opportunity. Kou expects the market for DRAM-equipped near-CPU boot drives to exceed $10 billion by 2030, with Silicon Motion targeting product ramps in the second half of 2027.

Story Continues

Silicon Motion Addresses Supply and Pricing Risks

During the analyst Q&A, B. Riley Securities questioned whether supply constraints could limit growth beyond management's 2027 expectations.

Kou responded that Silicon Motion has secured wafer capacity primarily through TSMC, alongside assembly, testing and substrate resources, to support its anticipated expansion.

William Blair analysts examined exposure to NAND pricing fluctuations. Kou explained that customer pricing arrangements generally span six months, helping manage costs. Chief financial officer Jason Tsai added that normalization of storage specifications and new customer programs could support growth even if NAND prices stabilize.

SIMO Details Funding and Consumer Market Pressures

Management acknowledged continuing weakness in smartphones and PCs as elevated memory prices pressure device affordability. Kou expects eMMC and UFS controller demand to remain relatively flat near term.

In contrast, PCIe Gen 5 controller adoption offers higher average selling prices and additional market share opportunities. Management expects the technology's PC market penetration to reach 20% to 25% by the end of 2027.

Responding to working-capital questions, Tsai said the company's $1.15 billion convertible-note financing should support anticipated funding requirements for the next couple of years. Inventory conversion remains an important consideration as solutions revenues expand.

Silicon Motion Focuses on More Diversified Growth

Management's overarching message centered on reducing dependence on consumer storage cycles through higher-value enterprise, automotive and AI applications.

Tsai emphasized that longer product lifecycles and multi-year customer engagements should improve business visibility. Management remains focused on scaling these opportunities while maintaining profitability and managing supply constraints.

What SIMO's Zacks Rank and Style Scores Indicate

SIMO currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), indicating favorable near-term earnings estimate revision trends. However, its Value Score of D and Growth and Momentum Scores of C reflect less compelling characteristics across individual investment styles. The stock's VGM Score of D further indicates that its combined value, growth and momentum characteristics are relatively weak. These scores temper the favorable Zacks Rank signal, as higher-ranked stocks with A or B Style Scores have historically demonstrated stronger performance potential.

news.Title: STM Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Growth and Margin Recovery
news.Content:
STMicroelectronics N.V. STM emphasized accelerating AI datacenter demand, improving industrial orders and manufacturing restructuring as central drivers of its growth outlook during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call.

Management highlighted strong bookings, expanding customer engagements and improving profitability, while analysts focused on the sustainability of demand, capacity constraints and the timing of anticipated margin improvements.

STM Sees Stronger Demand and Expanding Backlog

President and CEO Jean-Marc Chery said demand strengthened during the quarter, with the overall book-to-bill ratio exceeding 2. The ratio surpassed 3 in industrial and communication equipment and computer peripherals.

Chery reported that backlog exceeded $20 billion, representing approximately five quarters of revenues at the fourth-quarter guidance midpoint. Distribution inventories remained below standard targets.

Revenues increased 17.9% year over year to $3.76 billion, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.71 billion.

Reported earnings of 37 cents per share missed the consensus estimate of 40 cents.

STMicroelectronics N.V. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

STMicroelectronics N.V. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | STMicroelectronics N.V. Quote

STMicroelectronics Targets Accelerating AI Revenues

Chery projected approximately $1.3 billion in AI datacenter revenues for 2026, with ambitions to more than double that contribution in 2027.

During questioning from TD Cowen, Chery explained that approximately 85% of current datacenter revenues originate from the Microcontrollers, Digital ICs and RF Products Group.

Remi El-Ouazzane, president of that product group, expects datacenter microcontroller revenues to double in 2027. Silicon photonics should become a meaningful contributor, supported by capacity expansion exceeding fourfold year over year.

El-Ouazzane also expects BiCMOS design wins to deliver a more substantial revenue contribution beginning in 2028.

STM Outlines a Path Toward Higher Gross Margins

President and CFO Lorenzo Grandi reaffirmed the intermediate gross margin target of 44% to 46%, supported by manufacturing restructuring and improved product mix.

Grandi expects more than 400 basis points of structural margin improvement from transitioning production away from legacy facilities. Benefits should materialize toward late 2027 or early 2028, depending on factory closures and customer qualifications.

Responding to questions from TD Cowen and JPMorgan, Grandi clarified that the improvement depends on transferring production to larger, more automated wafer facilities.

Story Continues

He also identified rising input costs as a headwind, partially offset by manufacturing efficiencies and selective price increases.

STMicroelectronics Expects Industrial Growth to Continue

Chery highlighted industrial revenue growth of 40% year over year, driven by general-purpose microcontrollers, analog products and power conversion.

Automotive revenues increased 5%, supported by application-specific ICs, sensors and continued design-win activity.

During the Q&A, Chery expressed confidence in automotive growth during 2027, particularly in European electromobility and hybrid vehicles.

El-Ouazzane also highlighted expanding low Earth orbit satellite opportunities. He indicated that capacity availability, rather than customer demand, could constrain revenue growth.

STM Projects Further Revenue and Margin Expansion

Chery guided fourth-quarter revenues to approximately $4.15 billion, representing sequential growth of 10.5%, with gross margin expected near 39%.

Full-year revenues are projected at approximately $14.5 billion, up 22.8% year over year. Management expects full-year non-GAAP gross margin of 36.6%.

Grandi expects fourth-quarter non-GAAP operating expenses of approximately $1.035 billion. For 2027, he anticipates higher absolute expenses despite continued cost savings.

Management also expressed confidence in meeting first-quarter 2027 revenue consensus despite the shorter reporting calendar.

STMicroelectronics Maintains Focus on Execution

Management's commentary reflected confidence in sustained demand across AI infrastructure, industrial applications and satellite communications.

However, manufacturing transitions, input-cost inflation and capacity availability remain important operating considerations.

The company's priorities center on expanding strategic production capacity, completing factory restructuring and converting its growing backlog into revenues while improving profitability.

What STM's Zacks Rank and Style Scores Indicate

STM currently carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell), indicating an unfavorable near-term earnings estimate revision outlook. Its Growth Score of B reflects relatively favorable growth characteristics, while its Value Score of D indicates weaker valuation appeal. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

The stock's Momentum Score of C indicates moderate price momentum characteristics, while its composite VGM Score of D reflects an unfavorable overall combination of value, growth and momentum factors. Despite its favorable Growth Score, the Zacks Rank #4, combined with the weak VGM Score, points to limited near-term outperformance potential.

The Zacks Rank remains subject to change as analysts revise earnings estimates following the latest results and management commentary.

news.Title: Texas Instruments Inc's Dividend Analysis
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . A Closer Look at the Upcoming Payout, Dividend History, and Growth Outlook for the Semiconductor Leader Texas Instruments Inc ( NASDAQ:TXN ) recently announced a total dividend of $1.52 per share, with the ex-dividend date set for 2026-10-30. This amount consists of a $1.52 per share cash dividend payable on 2026-11-10. For income-focused investors, the ex-dividend date is a key marker: shareholders must own the stock before that date to qualify for the payment. As investors look forward to this upcoming distribution, the spotlight also shines on the company's dividend history, yield, and growth rates. Using data from GuruFocus, let's look into Texas Instruments Inc's dividend performance and assess its sustainability. What Does Texas Instruments Inc Do? Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with TXN. High Yield Dividend Stocks in Gurus' Portfolio This Powerful Chart Made Peter Lynch 29% A Year For 13 Years How to calculate the intrinsic value of a stock? Is TXN fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Texas Instruments designs and manufactures semiconductors sold to electronics designers and manufacturers worldwide, generating $17.68 billion of revenue in 2025. Its Analog segment (about 79% of revenue) supplies power management and signal chain chips that condition, amplify, convert, and manage electrical signals and power in nearly every type of electronic equipment; its Embedded Processing segment provides microcontrollers and processors. TI's portfolio exceeds 80,000 products serving industrial, automotive, personal electronics, data center, and communications markets, sold largely through its own direct channel. Its competitive advantages include internal manufacturing and technology, highlighted by a multi-year investment cycle in 300-millimeter wafer fabs in Texas and Utah, portfolio breadth, channel reach, and product longevity. Founded in 1930 and headquartered in Dallas, TI manages the business to maximize long-term free cash flow per share. A Glimpse at Texas Instruments Inc's Dividend History Texas Instruments Inc has maintained a consistent dividend payment record since 1985, and dividends are currently distributed on a quarterly basis. More importantly, the company has increased its dividend each year since 2001. The stock is thus listed as a dividend aristocrat, an honor given to companies that have raised their dividend each year for at least the past 25 years. For value investors, such a long record signals disciplined capital allocation and a management team committed to returning cash to shareholders through complete business cycles. Story Continues Below is a chart showing annual Dividends Per Share for tracking historical trends. Breaking Down Texas Instruments Inc's Dividend Yield and Growth As of today, Texas Instruments Inc currently has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 1.92% and a 12-month forward dividend yield of 2.04%. The gap between the two suggests an expectation of increased dividend payments over the next 12 months. The trailing yield reflects dividends actually paid over the past year, while the forward yield incorporates the most recent dividend rate annualized, so a higher forward figure implies the payout has recently been raised. Over the past three years, Texas Instruments Inc's annual dividend growth rate was 5.50%. Extended to a five-year horizon, this rate increased to 8.00% per year. And over the past decade, Texas Instruments Inc's annual dividends per share growth rate stands at an impressive 15.20%. This pattern of decelerating growth from the 10-year to the 3-year window is worth noting: it may reflect a more mature payout policy or a period of heavier capital investment in manufacturing capacity. Based on Texas Instruments Inc's dividend yield and five-year growth rate, the 5-year yield on cost of Texas Instruments Inc stock as of today is approximately 2.82%. Yield on cost estimates the effective return on today's investment after five years of assumed dividend growth, offering a forward-looking complement to the current yield. The Sustainability Question: Payout Ratio and Profitability To assess the sustainability of the dividend, one needs to evaluate the company's payout ratio. The dividend payout ratio provides insights into the portion of earnings the company distributes as dividends. A lower ratio suggests that the company retains a significant part of its earnings, thereby ensuring the availability of funds for future growth and unexpected downturns. As of 2026-09-30, Texas Instruments Inc's dividend payout ratio is 0.73. And this may suggest that the company's dividend may not be sustainable, since a ratio approaching three-quarters of earnings leaves a narrower cushion for reinvestment and adverse conditions. Texas Instruments Inc's profitability rank offers an understanding of the company's earnings prowess relative to its peers. GuruFocus ranks Texas Instruments Inc's profitability 8 out of 10 as of 2026-09-30, suggesting good profitability prospects. The company has reported positive net income for each year over the past decade, further solidifying its high profitability. This earnings consistency is an important counterweight when judging whether the current payout level can be maintained. Growth Metrics: The Future Outlook To ensure the sustainability of dividends, a company must have robust growth metrics. Texas Instruments Inc's growth rank of 8 out of 10 suggests that the company's growth trajectory is good relative to its competitors. However, the headline rank should be read alongside the underlying operating trends discussed below, which have been uneven in recent years amid a cyclical semiconductor downturn and heavy capital spending. Revenue is the lifeblood of any company, and Texas Instruments Inc's revenue per share , combined with the 3-year revenue growth rate , indicates a strong revenue model. Texas Instruments Inc's revenue has increased by approximately -3.60% per year on average, a rate that underperforms approximately 63.15% of global competitors. The negative figure reflects the recent industry correction rather than a structural loss of demand, but it does temper the growth picture. The company's 3-year EPS growth rate showcases its capability to grow its earnings, a critical component for sustaining dividends in the long run. During the past three years, Texas Instruments Inc's earnings increased by approximately -16.80% per year on average, a rate that underperforms approximately 67.5% of global competitors. Lastly, the company's 5-year EBITDA growth rate of -6.00% underperforms approximately 69.47% of global competitors. Next Steps for Dividend-Focused Investors Texas Instruments Inc's dividend story is one of strong foundations and near-term tension. On the positive side, the company has paid dividends since 1985, raised them every year since 2001, and holds dividend aristocrat status, backed by a profitability rank of 8 out of 10 and a decade of positive net income. The forward yield of 2.04% exceeding the trailing 1.92% points to continued increases, and a 5-year yield on cost of roughly 2.82% rewards patient holders. Yet a payout ratio of 0.73, combined with negative three-year revenue and EPS growth and a -6.00% five-year EBITDA trend, suggests the dividend consumes a meaningful share of earnings during the current downturn. For value investors, the key question is whether Texas Instruments Inc's long-term free cash flow per share can resume growth as analog demand recovers and the 300-millimeter fab investment cycle matures. A payout ratio near 0.73 is not alarming for a cyclical semiconductor leader, but it warrants monitoring alongside cash flow rather than earnings alone. Readers should watch upcoming quarterly reports for signs of revenue stabilization and capital spending discipline. news.Title: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Cisco Systems, Digi International and Lantronix
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 30, 2026 – Today, Zacks Equity Research discusses Cisco Systems CSCO, Digi International DGII and Lantronix LTRX.

Industry: Computer - Networking

Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/3017988/3-stocks-to-consider-from-a-flourishing-networking-industry

The Zacks Computer - Networking industry participants are expected to benefit from the networking infrastructure upgrade driven by AI workloads, cloud computing, big data, network security and next-generation connectivity.

The proliferation of AI workloads and hyperscale data centers is accelerating investments in high-speed interconnects, optical networking and Ethernet switches. Players in this space are focused on capitalizing on the multi-billion-dollar AI infrastructure opportunity. Increasing adoption of AI-driven applications across enterprises is also driving investments in next-gen networking infrastructure capable of supporting higher bandwidth, lower latency and heightened security requirements. Continued deployment of 5G, the proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT), industrial automation and edge computing is strengthening demand for reliable connectivity solutions. Increasing deployment of Wi-Fi 7 also presents a significant growth opportunity.

Also, the explosion of AI workloads requires a major upgrade to observability infrastructure. There is a greater need for continuous monitoring of hybrid environments and tighter security amid rising attacks. This will spur demand for innovative networking products, favoring prospects for prominent industry players such as Cisco Systems , Digi International and Lantronix .

However, cautious IT spending amid heightened uncertainty over global macroeconomic conditions and volatile supply-chain dynamics due to tariff troubles continues to be concerning for the participants in the near term. Fierce competition is an overhang on pricing power and margin expansion.

Industry Description

The Zacks Computer-Networking industry comprises companies that offer networking and Internet-connected products, including wireless (Wi-Fi and Long-Term Evolution or LTE), Ethernet and powerline, focusing on dependability and ease of use. The products are available in numerous configurations to cater to the changing requirements of consumers in each geographic territory where it operates.

Several industry players also provide mission-critical IoT solutions and network security services to help clients build next-generation connected products, and implement and manage critical communications infrastructures in demanding environments with enhanced safety levels. Focus on developing IoT sensors, drones and wearables amid increasing demand for cloud computing-based contact tracing applications is driving the industry.

Story Continues

4 Trends Influencing the Industry's Future

Technological Advancement Opening Business Avenues: The proliferation of generative AI, agentic AI and high adoption of cloud and data-intensive applications is driving higher traffic and creating a need for advanced optical networking, high-speed interconnects, Ethernet switches, routing and wireless infrastructure. The transition toward 800G and 1.6T networking technologies is expected to further drive infrastructure modernization and capacity expansion.

Expansion of industrial IoT and edge computing, and the increasing popularity of smart connected devices are further creating growth opportunities. Rising cybersecurity concerns are emerging as a key tailwind, driving demand for solutions such as threat detection, network monitoring and zero-trust security architectures.

Continued Deployment of 5G to Boost Growth Prospects: The continued expansion of the 5G technology hinges on substantial investments to upgrade infrastructure in the core fiber backhaul network to support growth in data services. Efforts to develop smart connected homes, hospitals, factories, buildings, cities and self-driving vehicles bode well for industry players. These firms invest heavily in LTE, broadband and fiber to provide additional capacity and improve Internet and wireless networks. These initiatives hold promise.

Wi-Fi 7 Upgrade Cycle to Drive Momentum: Brisk technological advancement, dynamic products, high-speed connectivity, low latency and evolving industry standards define the networking industry. The growing clout of the latest Wi-Fi 6E-compliant residential gateways, Wi-Fi routers, set-top boxes and wireless range extenders is a testament to the same.

The increasing demand for connecting more devices to the network has been driving demand for Wi-Fi 6E devices. Wi-Fi 6E addresses Wi-Fi spectrum shortage issues by providing continuous channel bandwidth to support a higher number of connected devices without compromising speed. The rollout of Wi-Fi 7 bodes well for the companies in this space.

Macroeconomic Turmoil Is Concerning: Global macroeconomic weakness and volatile supply-chain dynamics are persistent concerns. Tariff troubles, especially between the United States and China, remain an overhang on global supply chains. Inflation could affect spending across small and medium-sized businesses globally and uncertainty in business visibility could dent the industry's near-term performance.

The computer networking industry remains highly competitive, with a large number of established and new players vying for market share. As growth stabilizes, competition often intensifies, leading to pricing pressure and margin compression.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Bright Near-Term Prospects

The Zacks Computer-Networking Industry is housed within the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. The industry carries a Zacks Industry Rank #75, positioning it in the top 30% of more than 247 Zacks industries.

The group's Zacks Industry Rank, which is the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates bright near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than two to one.

Before we present a few stocks you may want to consider for your portfolio, considering bright prospects, let us look at the industry's recent stock-market performance and valuation picture

Industry Outperforms the S&P 500 and the Sector

The Zacks Computer-Networking industry has outperformed the S&P 500 composite and the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector in the past year.

The industry has gained 51.9% over this period, compared with the broader sector's 13.4% rally. The S&P 500 has appreciated 13.3% over the same time frame.

Industry's Current Valuation

Based on the forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, a common multiple for valuing Computer-Networking stocks, the industry is currently trading at 24.62X, compared with the S&P 500's 19.27X. It is also higher than the sector's forward-12-month P/E of 19.25X.

In the past five years, the industry traded as high as 31.47X and as low as 12.45X, with the median being 17.27X.

3 Computer-Networking Stocks to Add to Your Portfolio

Cisco Systems: Headquartered in San Jose, CA, the company offers identity and access, advanced threat and unified threat management solutions.

Cisco is benefiting from the demand for AI Infrastructure solutions, with hyperscaler demand acting as a key catalyst. The company expects AI infrastructure revenues from hyperscalers to reach $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027.

Strong demand for its Silicon One based systems and Acacia optical networking solutions is expected to support growth. Fiscal 2026 hyperscaler AI orders were about 60% Silicon One-based systems and 40% optics. Acacia generated more than $1 billion in orders in the fiscal fourth quarter.

On the last earnings call, CSCO noted that accelerating agentic AI is driving a "networking super cycle" resulting in increasing demand for its Networking stack to support inferencing across cloud, on-premise and edge environments. In October, Cisco announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to develop an open industry specification for next-generation 400G-per-lane pluggable optics, further strengthening its position in the evolving AI networking ecosystem.

For fiscal 2027, Cisco projects revenues of $72.2-$73.4 billion and non-GAAP earnings of $5.05-$5.11 per share. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 bottom line is pinned at $5.11, unchanged in the past 30 days. Shares have gained 51.3% in the past year.

At present, CSCO carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Lantronix : Based in Irvine, CA, Lantronix specializes in providing Industrial and Edge AI IoT solutions for high-growth applications in certain verticals, including enterprise IT, smart cities and commercial and defense unmanned systems.

The company's unmanned systems business has emerged as a meaningful growth driver. Revenues from Unmanned systems came in at $12.6 million in fiscal 2026 and management expects the segment to represent 15% to 20% of total revenues in fiscal 2027. Increasing adoption of AI-enabled drones and counter-UAS applications across defense, industrial and commercial applications presents significant opportunities for its unmanned systems business.  The recent inclusion of its Open-Q 8550CS system-on-module in the Blue UAS Framework strengthens its ability to serve U.S. defense drone manufacturers.

The company also introduced the Spotter edge AI computing platform, which expands its offerings for autonomous drones and robotics.

Beyond unmanned systems, the IoT System Solutions is witnessing improving conditions after federal government shutdowns led to extended procurement cycles. The tuck-in acquisition of Vecima Networks' Industrial IoT business, including the Nero Global Tracking platform, is also expanding its recurring software revenue base.

However, tightening memory availability and rising costs remain concerns, while the increasing contribution from relatively lower-margin unmanned systems solutions could weigh on profitability.

At present, LTRX carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 earnings is 22 cents per share, unchanged in the past 60 days. Shares have gained 23.8% in the past year.

Digi International: Based in Hopkins, MN, Digi is a well-known provider of business and mission-critical Internet of Things (IoT) products and services globally. The company's industrial Internet of Things offerings encompass embedded, edge and turnkey vertical solutions. These solutions find applications across emerging technology trends such as AI, edge computing and industrial automation. The company is embedding AI across its portfolio.

Digi's outlook remains supported by sustained ARR growth, ongoing benefits from acquisitions and the long-term opportunity to integrate AI into industrial IoT solutions. The company expects ARR to grow 27% in fiscal 2026, up from 25% projected earlier.

To capitalize on the AI opportunity, DGII had unveiled DANI, the Digi Artificial Network Intelligence agent, earlier in the year. DANI is an AI network operations agent that is embedded in Digi Remote Manager, a networking device management platform, enabling network operators/managed service providers to monitor issues, identify causes and offer recommended actions through a unified conversational interface.

The recent launch of Digi EX60, an enterprise 5G router integrating Wi-Fi 7 and AI-assisted network management capabilities, further strengthens its offerings for distributed enterprise networks.

Digi continues to pursue strategic acquisitions, which are likely to supplement organic growth. The proposed acquisition of Disruptive Technologies is expected to expand the capabilities and reach of its SmartSense platform. The company expects the transaction to contribute approximately $9 million in additional adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow in fiscal 2028. The transaction is expected to close before the end of 2026, subject to regulatory approval.

On the last earnings call, management highlighted challenges in the supply chain, which could exert pressure on margins.

At present, DGII carries a Zacks Rank #3. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 bottom line is pegged at $3.17, unchanged in the past 60 days. Shares have gained 106% in the past year.

news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Revenue: $560 million, up 24% sequentially and 131% year-over-year; fourth consecutive record quarter, above guidance of $519M$541M.

Gross Margin: 53.7%, significantly above guidance on favorable product mix and better-than-expected Ferri automotive margins.

Operating Expenses: $120.7 million, slightly down sequentially.

Operating Margin: 32.1%, well above guidance.

Earnings Per ADS: $4.35, up 79% sequentially and 333% year-over-year.

Stock-Based Compensation: $17.3 million (excluded from non-GAAP results).

Cash and Equivalents: $953.6 million (including restricted cash), up from $181.8 million at end of Q2.

Convertible Bond Issuance: $1.15 billion aggregate ($1.127 billion net proceeds), 0% interest, initial conversion price of $380.5 (65% premium).

Solutions Business (Ferri/Automotive, Edge AI, Boot Drive): Revenue up over 75% sequentially, representing over 40% of total revenue.

eMMC/UFS Business: Up over 100% year-over-year in first half of 2026; declined modestly sequentially in Q3 on customer launch timing and smartphone OEM cost pressure.

SSD Controller Business: Strong sequential and year-over-year growth; PCIe 5 controllers ~10% of PC market, expected to reach 20%25% by end of 2027.

Q4 Revenue Guidance: $588 million$616 million, up 5%10% sequentially.

Q4 Operating Margin Guidance: 36%37%.

Q4 Tax Rate Guidance: 20% effective tax rate; stock-based comp and dispute-related expenses of $34.6M$35.6M.

Full-Year 2026 Outlook: Record revenue, more than doubling year-over-year (over 100% top-line growth); operating margin to exceed 30% exiting the year.

2027 Outlook: Revenue growth of at least 40%; gross margin in low-to-mid 50% range.

Release Date: October 29, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

Silicon Motion Technology Corp ( NASDAQ:SIMO ) delivered record Q3 2026 revenue of $560 million, up 24% sequentially and 131% year-over-year, exceeding guidance.

Gross margin reached 53.7%, significantly above guidance, driven by better product mix and higher margins in Ferri automotive products.

Earnings per ADS was $4.35, a 79% sequential increase and 333% year-over-year increase.

The company expects 2026 revenue to more than double year-over-year and projects at least 40% revenue growth in 2027 with gross margins in the low-to-mid 50% range.

Strong momentum in enterprise and automotive segments: MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers on track with all seven announced customers ramping in 2026, and Ferri automotive revenue up over 75% sequentially, representing over 40% of total revenue.

The company secured 2027 wafer supply from TSMC, as well as test and assembly capacity, supporting its growth outlook.

New opportunities in near-CPU boot drives with DRAM, estimated to be a $10 billion market by 2030, with production ramp expected in second-half 2027.

Story Continues

Negative Points

Silicon Motion Technology Corp ( NASDAQ:SIMO ) faces near-term headwinds in its eMMC/UFS controller business due to challenging smartphone OEM demand amid higher NAND and DRAM prices, with revenue expected to remain relatively flat.

The PC and smartphone markets remain weak, with consumer unit volumes declining as OEMs struggle to offer affordable devices amid rising memory and storage costs.

The company expects SSD controller business to be flat to slightly down in Q4 2026 due to current memory and storage environment and typical seasonality.

NAND supply remains tight, and the company anticipates the supply-demand imbalance to persist, with new NAND fabs not planned until 2028.

The arbitration with a key customer (likely Micron) is still pending, creating uncertainty.

The company has limited R&D resources to pursue all opportunities, particularly in the near-CPU boot drive market, which may slow time-to-market.

Working capital needs are increasing, with inventory growing to support growth, though the recent $1.15 billion convertible bond offering provides funding for the next couple of years.

Q & A Highlights

Q : Given the guidance for at least 40% revenue growth next year and gross margin in the low-to-mid 50% range, what are the main drivers? A : CFO Jason Tsai attributed the outlook to significant traction in MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers and aggressive ramping of Ferri automotive solutions, which are multi-year engagements with long product cycles. He noted that based on backlog and anticipated growth from Titan, SSD controllers, and Ferri automotive, the company believes it can sustain low-to-mid 50% gross margins.

Q : Can you discuss the near-CPU boot drive opportunity with DRAM, including the size of the market and the ramp timeline? A : CEO Wallace Kou stated that NAND makers are deprioritizing low-capacity near-CPU boot drives (1TB-2TB) as they focus on high-capacity SSDs, creating a significant shortage. He estimates this market will reach at least $10 billion by 2030. Silicon Motion expects firmware and solutions ready by early Q1 2027, with production ramping in the second half of 2027, leveraging its existing controller technology with built-in OCP features.

Q : How is Silicon Motion positioned with wafer supply, packaging, and test capacity to support 40% growth next year, and is there upside potential? A : CEO Wallace Kou acknowledged industry-wide shortages across substrates, materials, wafers, NAND, and test capacity. However, he stated the manufacturing team secured 2027 wafer supply primarily with TSMC, along with test capacity, assembly capacity, and substrate materials. He expressed confidence in supporting at least 40% year-over-year growth, with more detailed 2027 guidance to come next quarter.

Q : As the SSD solution business grows to over 40% of revenue, how do you manage NAND pricing exposure, particularly if NAND prices decline? A : CEO Wallace Kou explained that Silicon Motion negotiates six-month pricing contracts with customers, passing through NAND cost increases while maintaining margin protection. He expects NAND price increases to moderate as spot prices become challenging for module makers. CFO Jason Tsai added that if NAND availability and pricing improve, customers would likely double density, and re-specing to normal specs plus new customer opportunities position the company to grow even as the NAND market stabilizes.

Q : What is the revenue mix between solutions (Ferri, Boot Drive, automotive) and controllers, and how will it change next year? A : CEO Wallace Kou stated that approximately 40% of total revenue came from solutions (boot drive, automotive) and 60% from controllers in Q3. He expects the mix to become more balanced at roughly 50/50 next year as automotive solutions grow.

Q : With enterprise and Ferri becoming a larger portion of the business, should we expect consumer seasonality from Q4 to Q1 to diminish? A : CFO Jason Tsai confirmed that as enterprise and Ferri become bigger portions of the mix, normal consumer seasonality will be more muted going forward since the consumer business is becoming a smaller percentage of total revenue. He deferred specific Q1 and 2027 guidance to January.

Q : Can you provide an update on the Singapore arbitration? A : CFO Jason Tsai stated that closing arguments in the Singapore arbitration were held in March, and the company is still awaiting results. He declined to provide additional comments until the outcome is announced.

Q : How should we think about gross margins for the solutions business as NAND prices stabilize, and what working capital is needed to support 50%+ growth in solutions? A : CFO Jason Tsai explained that six-month pricing contracts and tight inventory turns provide margin protection. Automotive products are qualified for multi-year projects (3-5 years) with pricing and supply agreements set at the outset, supporting better margins given the solution complexity and support requirements. Regarding working capital, he stated the $1.15 billion convertible bond raise is sufficient to fund the next couple of years of business based on current forecasts, with inventory growing in Q4 before turning back into cash flow.

Q : What is Silicon Motion's strategy in China regarding NAND makers, CSPs, and competition? A : CEO Wallace Kou emphasized balancing China and the rest of the world, collaborating with YMTC directly and through module makers, and growing local China R&D to support China customers while Taiwan supports U.S. and global customers. He noted that Chinese enterprise controller companies that previously bought NAND at cyclical lows and sold drives at highs are now struggling in a non-cyclical pricing environment. Silicon Motion's strategy is to win NAND maker design wins, hyperscaler customers in both the U.S. and China, and CSPs directly, while selling controllers and firmware through module maker and NAND maker partners.

Q : How do you view the competitive landscape for enterprise controllers in China? A : CEO Wallace Kou stated that while one or two Chinese companies have moved toward IPOs, he does not see them as strong enough to compete long-term on technology or business model. He expressed confidence in Silicon Motion's position, citing its strong development pipeline for PCIe Gen 5 and Gen 6 controllers.

Q : Has the convertible bond issuance changed the dividend policy or capital structure targets? A : CFO Jason Tsai said capital allocation priorities remain unchanged: dividend, opportunistic share buybacks, and M&A as appropriate. The company recently increased its dividend to $2.30 per ADS per year and has a 10-year history of raising it. He noted working capital needs are increasing, and the convertible bond raise puts the company in a better position to drive growth with improved working capital.

Q : What is the outlook for MonTitan demand, particularly regarding HBM/DRAM innovations and KV cache requirements per GPU? A : CEO Wallace Kou said MonTitan demand comes from a wide range of customers including AI server, hyperscalers, CSPs, and the NVIDIA ecosystem. He noted compute SSD demand was larger this year due to high NAND prices, but high-capacity QLC momentum is building for next year as NAND makers ramp 2-terabit QLC production. He expects NVIDIA to redefine minimum KV cache capacity per GPU early next year, and growing KV cache demand will drive additional enterprise SSD and controller demand.

news.Title: STMicroelectronics NV (STM) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Highlights: Revenue Tops Guidance as AI Data ...
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Net Revenue: $3.76 billion in Q3 2026, above the midpoint of the business outlook range.

Gross Profit: $1.40 billion, up 32.2% year-over-year.

Gross Margin: 37.3%, up 410 basis points year-over-year and 250 basis points sequentially; included ~60 bps unused capacity charges and ~40 bps non-recurring reshaping costs.

Operating Income: $367 million (GAAP), including $55 million impairment/restructuring charges and $7 million PPA effects.

Non-U.S. GAAP Operating Income: $429 million, with non-U.S. GAAP operating margin of 11.4%.

Segment Operating Margins: Analog, MEMS & Sensors 14.1%; Power & Discrete negative 17.1%; Embedded Processing 23.1%; RF & Optical Communications 26.2%.

Net Income: $291 million (GAAP), versus $237 million a year ago.

Diluted EPS: $0.31 (GAAP) versus $0.26 a year ago; non-U.S. GAAP diluted EPS $0.37.

Non-U.S. GAAP Net Income: $344 million.

Automotive Revenue: Stable sequentially, up 5% year-over-year.

Industrial Revenue: Up 12% sequentially and 40% year-over-year.

Personal Electronics Revenue: Up 12% sequentially, down 4% year-over-year.

Communication Equipment & Computer Peripherals Revenue: Up 14% sequentially and 64% year-over-year.

Segment Revenue Growth (YoY): Analog, MEMS & Sensors +8.8%; Power & Discrete +11.3%; Embedded Processing +24.1%; RF & Optical Communications +46.2%.

OEM & Distribution Sales: Up 10.2% and 38.8% year-over-year, respectively.

AI Data Center Revenue: ~$1.3 billion expected for 2026; ambition of well above $2 billion in 2027.

Story Continues
