Release Date: October 29, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

Q3 2026 net revenues of $3.76 billion exceeded the midpoint of guidance, driven by strength in communication equipment and computer peripherals.

Book-to-bill ratio remained well above one overall and significantly above two in communication equipment, computer peripherals, and industrial, indicating strong demand.

Industrial revenues grew 12% sequentially and 40% year-over-year, with broad-based design wins across automation, robotics, and power systems.

AI data center revenue is expected to reach about $1.3 billion in 2026 and well above $2 billion in 2027, with silicon photonics and MCUs driving growth.

Gross margin improved 410 basis points year-over-year to 37.3%, and management outlined a clear path to 44-46% target model through manufacturing reshaping and mix improvement.

Negative Points

Automotive revenues were flat sequentially, and personal electronics revenues declined 4% year-over-year, reflecting continued softness in consumer markets.

Gross margin remains below the target model, with temporary headwinds from unused capacity charges and non-recurring costs related to manufacturing reshaping.

Power and discrete segment reported an operating margin of negative 17.1%, impacted by the transition to 200mm wafers and legacy fab costs.

Input cost inflation is expected to be a headwind for gross margin, partially offsetting improvements from mix and pricing.

Q1 2027 revenue visibility is limited, with only 86 calendar days and typical seasonality, though management expects to meet consensus.

Q & A Highlights

Q : Can you clarify the timing and magnitude of the ~400 basis points of structural gross margin improvement from the manufacturing reshaping program? Will it hit all at once, and how does it fit with the path to the 44%-46% target model? A : CFO Lorenzo Grandi explained that the positive impact from reshaping the manufacturing footprint will become visible once the four legacy fabs are closed, expected toward the end of 2027 and into early 2028, and depends partly on customer qualification for three of the steps. He added that gross margin should still improve progressively each quarter from better mix, lower unused capacity charges, and reduced temporary transfer costs. Management targets the 44%-46% model and said it would update guidance in January and through next year, without committing to exceeding the target model despite strong AI-related mix.

Q : What is the outlook for the AI data center business in 2027, including the split between MCUs, silicon photonics, bipolar-CMOS and power? A : CEO Jean-Marc Chery said data center revenue will be about $1.3 billion in 2026, with more than 85% from MCUs, silicon photonics and electronic ICs, and will be "well above doubling" in 2027, with more detail to come in January. Remy Elwazan added that silicon photonics will become very relevant next year, contributing tens of percent of the total, while bipolar-CMOS wins will be mainly visible from 2028 onward, though non-negligible in 2027.

Q : What is the current backlog and visibility, and how should we think about 2027 seasonality given the shifting mix? A : Chery said book-to-bill was well above 2 overall, above 1 in every end market, and well above 3 in communication equipment/computer peripherals and industrial. Backlog is now well above $20 billion, equal to about five quarters of revenue at the Q4 midpoint, though still below the 2022-2023 peak. He noted 2027 seasonality will differ because the vertical mix is rebalancing, with automotive about 35% of revenue, industrial 22%-24%, communication/computer peripherals slightly above 20%, and personal electronics 22%, with communication/computer peripherals expected to keep growing.

Q : Can you give more color on the low Earth orbit satellite business for next year, including demand, customer base and capacity constraints? A : Remy Elwazan said 2026 was a record year for the satellite business on fast growth from the major customer, and he expects 2027 revenue to be the same or better, with additional customers ramping on top. He said ST is likely to be capacity-gated next year and is working to release more capacity, adding that its front-end module and bipolar-CMOS technologies have no close competitor given their noise-figure and spectrum-efficiency advantages.

Q : What is the outlook for automotive in 2027, including electromobility and silicon carbide? A : Chery said visibility from European Tier 1 customers has been stable for more than six months, and ST expects automotive to grow slightly above 10% for full-year 2026, roughly in line with the market. Power and discrete growth in Q4 will be well above 20%-25%, driven by European electromobility. For 2027, automotive should contribute roughly in line with the company average, while AI data centers and industrial remain the main growth drivers and consumer stays soft. Silicon carbide will grow about 20% this year and see another year of significant growth in 2027, helped by the conversion to 8-inch wafers at Catania and Shanxi.

Q : What is the status of the silicon photonics ramp in terms of yields and capacity expansion? A : Remy Elwazan said ST is ahead of plan, with customer electro-optical yields setting a new industry bar, and noted ST is the only at-scale 12-inch player shipping now, which supports critical-dimension and yield entitlement. He said the 2026 contribution is meaningful but far below next year's, when capacity will increase about 4x year on year, slightly more in practice, and described silicon photonics as a long growth story with long-term visibility.

Q : What is the direction for Q1 2027 gross margin and revenue, given the 86 calendar days in the quarter? A : Grandi said he would not formally guide Q1 gross margin but expects it to be at least at the current consensus level. Chery added that despite only 86 days in Q1, ST is comfortable delivering at least the revenue consensus for the quarter. Grandi also flagged input cost inflation as a headwind, offset by manufacturing efficiency, better mix and some price increases.

Q : What are the early indications from pricing negotiations with Tier 1 customers for next year? A : Grandi said ST is raising prices on selected products given higher input costs and longer lead times, and that if the supply-demand gap persists, 2027 pricing could be stable to slightly up. He cautioned that negotiations for next year are not yet complete, so it is too early to comment further.

Q : Was the better-than-expected personal electronics revenue in Q3 driven by a pull-in, and what does that mean for Q1? A : Chery said there was no specific pull-in; ST simply delivered customer demand, and personal electronics revenue came in better than expected, up 12% sequentially. He did not signal any risk of a Q1 payback from the Q3 strength.

Q : Why did margins decline year over year in analog/MEMS/sensors and power and discrete despite strong revenue growth, and what is the split of the 400 basis point improvement? A : Grandi said the over-400 basis point improvement combines larger wafer size, moving from poorly automated legacy fabs with high labor costs to more automated facilities, and it is complex to split the contributors. The analog/MEMS/sensors segment is suffering most in the transition phase from legacy fab transfers, with extra costs and lower efficiency, but should benefit most once production moves to the advanced 300mm fabs, while power and discrete will benefit from the move to 200mm.

Q : What is the OpEx outlook for 2027? A : Grandi said OpEx will go up next year but by less than sales, improving the operating expense-to-sales ratio.

news.Title: What Silicon Motion Technology (SIMO) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Silicon Motion Technology Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

Record Q3 performance: Revenue surged 131% year over year to $560 million, beating guidance, while non-GAAP earnings per ADS rose 333% to $4.35. Growth was led by automotive Ferri products, enterprise boot drives, and SSD controllers.

Automotive and enterprise markets are reshaping the business: Storage solutions revenue grew more than 75% sequentially and exceeded 40% of total revenue. MonTitan enterprise controllers are gaining customer traction, with all seven announced customers expected to begin commercial ramps in 2026.

Strong outlook despite weak consumer demand: Silicon Motion forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $588 million to $616 million and expects 2027 revenue growth of at least 40%. Management said expanding automotive and enterprise exposure should reduce reliance on challenged PC and smartphone markets.

3 Overlooked Tech Names Quietly Powering Everyday Life

Silicon Motion Technology (NASDAQ:SIMO) reported record third-quarter revenue and said its expanding automotive, enterprise storage and AI-related businesses are reducing its reliance on consumer device cycles.

Revenue for the September quarter rose 24% sequentially and 131% from a year earlier to $560 million, exceeding the company's guidance range of $519 million to $541 million. Non-GAAP gross margin was 53.7%, while non-GAAP earnings per ADS reached $4.35, up 79% sequentially and 333% year over year, according to CFO Jason Tsai.

→ Apple's Foldable iPhone Sold Out in Minutes, But Wall Street Has Questions

These 3 AI Stocks Just Crushed Earnings: Still Time To Buy?

"We delivered an outstanding third quarter, surpassing our expectations, driven by stronger execution and demand trends," Tsai said. The company recorded its fourth consecutive quarter of record revenue, with growth across most businesses led by Ferri automotive products, enterprise boot drives, and Edge and MonTitan SSD controllers.

Automotive and enterprise products drive mix shift

President and CEO Wallace Kou said Silicon Motion's storage solutions segment, which includes Ferri products and boot drives, produced its strongest quarterly result. Segment revenue rose more than 75% sequentially and represented more than 40% of total company revenue in the third quarter.

→ Off-Price, High-Yield: Why Ross Stores Is Defying the Retail Slump

Analysts Are All In on This Tech Stock—Why You Should Be, Too

The company said automotive products were a particular source of strength, benefiting from its portfolio of automotive-grade storage controllers and firmware. Kou said Silicon Motion has spent more than a decade developing automotive products and certifications, and that its automotive backlog has expanded as it gains share.

Story Continues

Silicon Motion also sees opportunities to apply Ferri products in robotics, drones and advanced networking equipment. Kou said the robotics market remains at an early stage and current volumes are small, but the company is engaged with several potential customers in humanoid robots and other physical AI applications. Tsai added that automotive-grade capabilities such as tolerance for high temperatures and vibration could provide an advantage in robotics.

→ Coca-Cola Stock Is Everything AI Isn't—And That's Its Biggest Strength

Enterprise boot drives are also becoming a larger part of the company's strategy. Kou said Silicon Motion won designs with several new Tier 1 customers in networking and AI infrastructure during the third quarter. Those programs are expected to ramp over the next two years.

The company estimates the enterprise boot-drive market will be about $3 billion in 2026 and exceed $5 billion by 2030. It also identified a separate opportunity in near-CPU boot drives that use onboard DRAM, which it estimates could surpass $10 billion by 2030. Silicon Motion expects to begin ramping products for that market in the second half of 2027, subject to customer and supply-chain execution.

MonTitan enterprise controller ramp continues

Silicon Motion said its MonTitan enterprise SSD controller business is gaining traction with NAND manufacturers, hyperscalers, cloud service providers and module makers. The company said its first two customers began shipping TLC enterprise SSDs for compute applications using MonTitan controllers in the second quarter.

All seven announced customers remain on track to begin commercial ramps during 2026, according to Kou. In the near term, the company expects TLC-based compute SSDs to ramp faster than QLC-based data-storage SSDs, until broader availability of 2-terabit QLC NAND dies.

During the third quarter, Silicon Motion taped out its next-generation 4-nanometer PCIe 6 MonTitan controller. The product is intended for hyperscalers and cloud service providers, with sampling expected in the first quarter of 2027. Kou said the company has one design involving multiple Tier 1 customers, including NAND makers, hyperscalers and cloud providers.

In its Edge SSD controller business, Silicon Motion reported sequential and year-over-year growth. The company said PCIe 5 products are gaining adoption in PCs and currently account for about 10% of the PC market. Kou said the company expects PCIe 5 penetration to reach 20% to 25% by the end of 2027, supporting higher average selling prices as the market transitions from PCIe 4.

Consumer markets remain challenged

Management said higher memory and storage prices continue to pressure PC and smartphone makers, which are trying to offer affordable products amid rising NAND and DRAM costs. Silicon Motion's eMMC and UFS revenue declined modestly from the prior quarter because of customer launch timing and difficult smartphone conditions.

The company expects eMMC and UFS revenue to remain relatively flat in the near term. However, Kou said new UFS 4.1 and UFS 5 controllers could support growth next year and beyond through higher average selling prices.

While the broader consumer environment remains difficult, Silicon Motion said its increasing exposure to automotive and enterprise applications should make traditional consumer seasonality less pronounced. Tsai said consumer cycles will have less influence on results as enterprise and Ferri products become a larger part of the business.

Fourth-quarter and 2027 outlook

For the fourth quarter, Silicon Motion forecast revenue of $588 million to $616 million, representing sequential growth of 5% to 10%. Management expects growth across nearly all product segments, led by Ferri automotive products, enterprise boot-drive solutions and MonTitan enterprise controllers.

The company expects its SSD controller business to be flat to slightly lower sequentially, reflecting memory and storage market conditions and typical seasonal patterns. Silicon Motion projected fourth-quarter gross margin of 54% to 55% and operating margin of 36% to 37%.

For 2026, management said revenue is on track to more than double from the prior year and operating margin is expected to exceed 30% exiting the year. Looking ahead, Tsai said Silicon Motion expects revenue to grow by at least 40% in 2027, supported by backlog across its businesses. The company expects gross margin to remain in the low-to-mid-50% range as enterprise controllers and Ferri automotive products account for more of its mix.

Silicon Motion also highlighted its August convertible-note offering, which raised $1.15 billion in aggregate principal amount and generated $1.127 billion in net proceeds. The company ended the third quarter with $953.6 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash. Tsai said the capital raise is expected to fund working-capital needs for the next several years based on current forecasts, while helping the company support inventory growth and business expansion.

About Silicon Motion Technology (NASDAQ:SIMO)

Silicon Motion Technology Corporation is a fabless semiconductor company that designs, develops and markets NAND flash storage controllers. Its products manage the storage, performance, reliability and power consumption of data stored in NAND flash memory and are used in a range of consumer, mobile, computing and industrial applications.

The company's product portfolio includes controllers for solid-state drives (SSDs), embedded storage products such as eMMC and UFS devices, and other flash-based storage solutions.

news.Title: Got $1,000? This Monster Growth Stock Is on Sale Right Now and Targets 10X Sales Growth By 2031
news.Content:
Marvell Technologies (MRVL) stock surged by more than 200% in the first two quarters of the year before stagnating, and it hasn't quite recovered since. The stock is currently 34% below its 52-week high, even though Marvell is one of the top artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor companies and a major supplier to data centers.

Marvell has also increased its fiscal 2031 revenue target of $70 billion to $90 billion, which is roughly 10 times its fiscal 2026 revenue at the midpoint. At this pace, it's easy to see why MRVL stock has done so well. Accordingly, the correction over the past few months should be short-lived, if Marvell can live up to expectations and data-center spending continues to rise.

More News from Barchart

Elon Musk Invests $1 Billion in Skydance Stock. He Could Be Setting the Stage for a Major Starlink Deal.

'I Still Live A Great Life': Floyd Mayweather Says a Man 'Acting Like He Was A Friend' Stole $200 Million From Him

MRVL Stock Sinks as Marvell Technology Reportedly Considers Acquiring Lumentum

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

Semiconductors Are Set to Remain in Demand

Semiconductor companies like Nvidia (NVDA), Broadcom (AVGO), and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) have surged above and beyond what anyone would have expected just two years ago. What's more, their demand is expected to stay in hyper-growth mode as AI companies continue building out data centers, and it's the semiconductor companies themselves that are successfully fueling this growth by funding AI startups.

This "circular" financing is not so doom and gloom as long as Wall Street keeps funding it. For the past few years, the market has been happy to pay up due to growth targets consistently being shattered and AI companies not hitting a wall. The upcoming Anthropic (ANT) initial public offering (IPO) is set to pull in even more money, supercharging the AI wave with fresh capital.

For Marvell, this means more potential demand and growth.

Why I'd Buy the Dip in Marvell Here

Analysts expect revenue to surge from $8.2 billion in fiscal 2026 to $19.7 billion in fiscal 2028, and that estimate could be surpassed if the AI spending spree continues. Semiconductor margins are expected to hold, as they have held up remarkably well in the past four years. New capacity entering the market hasn't been able to pull down prices due to demand outstripping supply. Thus, it would be premature to say we've hit a top.

Story Continues

I wouldn't buy MRVL stock if either the Anthropic IPO or a potential OpenAI IPO dramatically underperform expectations. If that happens, we'll likely see the "circular" financing start to slow down and reverse as fresh capital from the market dries up and eventually affects semiconductor manufacturers downstream.

But nothing yet says that investors' appetite for AI is weak. If anything, I expect both Anthropic and eventually OpenAI to repeat the SpaceX (SPCX) IPO; the stocks will likely initially over-perform, raise massive amounts of cash, perhaps tread water for a brief period, then surge as the freshly raised IPO cash helps boost growth.

Betting on Semiconductors Is Smart

Semiconductor stocks are trading at somewhat reasonable multiples when you consider the tremendous growth. MRVL stock trades at 79.8 times forward earnings, which is far from cheap. But a company that's guiding a 10 times sales increase in the next five years should trade much higher in any market environment.

That said, MRVL stock is among the most expensive semiconductor picks. If you don't want to dabble in a stock that just popped off last year, you can still stick with NVDA stock, for example. Overall, I expect most semiconductor stocks to keep climbing, including Marvell Technologies stock.

Analysts have been hiking their estimates for MRVL stock. The average price target of $337.05 suggests potential upside of 54% from current levels. Overall, Marvell stock has a consensus "Strong Buy" rating on Wall Street based on 39 analysts with coverage.

news.Title: Stock Market Today, Oct. 29: Marvell Falls on Lumentum Acquisition Talks
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL), a data infrastructure semiconductors provider, closed at $218.34 on Oct. 29, down a whopping 13.24%. The stock fell after reports surfaced that the company was in advanced talks to buy Lumentum Holdings , as investors weigh financing and integration risks.

Trading volume reached 40.4 million shares, coming in about 87% above its three-month average of 21.6 million shares. Marvell Technology IPO'd in 2000 and has grown 1,442% since going public.

How the markets moved today

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) closed at 7,720, down 0.31%, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) finished at 26,185, down 1.38%. Among semiconductor peers, Broadcom closed at $345.00, down 1.94%, and Nvidia closed at $213.66, down 0.80%, as chipmakers traded lower in a soft session for data infrastructure names.

What this means for investors

On Thursday, Oct. 29, reports surfaced that Marvell was in advanced talks to acquire Lumentum, a specialist in in lasers and high-speed optical components that are critical to powering AI data centers. Lumentum stock was up 0.61% to $919.53 at the close.

The rumors kept Marvell shares under pressure, with investors focused on financing and dilution risk. The deal is said to be an all-stock transaction that could value the combination as one of the largest global tech industry mergers of the year.

A final agreement has not yet been officially reached, but sources indicate a deal could be formally announced as early as next week. If true, gaining Lumentum positions Marvell to be a major player in the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom.

In its investor day conference on Oct. 6, Marvell raised its revenue outlook for its 2028 fiscal year (FY), ended Jan. 31, 2028, to $20 billion. Moreover, it revealed a FY2031 target of $70 billion to $90 billion in sales, and an earnings per share (EPS) target of $30 or more, far above its FY2026 diluted earnings of $3.07 per share. Adding Lumentum would only bolster these impressive numbers.

news.Title: Not Nvidia. Not AMD. This Custom AI Chip Designer Could Outperform Both by 2030.
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) are two of the biggest beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution. As big tech invests hundreds of billions of dollars in data centers , demand for semiconductors continues to accelerate.

However, another chipmaker could deliver even greater returns over the next several years: Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL). Interestingly, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang recognizes Marvell's potential. During the Computex conference in June, Huang called Marvell the next potential trillion-dollar company. Nvidia has even invested $2 billion in Marvell, reinforcing its confidence in the company.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Now, Marvell is reportedly exploring an acquisition that could supercharge its position in the AI infrastructure market. Let's dig into what makes Marvell unique and assess why the stock could be a compelling buy for long-term investors.

What role does Marvell play in the AI chip stack?

Nvidia and AMD primarily design general-purpose AI accelerators, known as GPUs. Marvell specializes in designing custom application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs). These processors are tailored to specific workloads, potentially offering superior training and inference performance, energy efficiency, and economics compared with off-the-shelf chips.

This value proposition appeals to hyperscalers such as Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms . Rather than relying exclusively on products from Nvidia and AMD, big tech is also investing in custom silicon designed around their own AI models. Marvell is positioning itself as a partner in this transition.

Marvell's opportunity extends beyond custom chips. Its portfolio also includes optical digital signal processors (DSPs) , Ethernet switches, high-speed interconnects, and silicon photonics. These products help move data between larger clusters of GPUs and memory. As AI models evolve and use cases become more sophisticated, Marvell's services should see increased demand.

Is Marvell acquiring Lumentum?

On Oct. 28, Reuters reported that Marvell was in advanced discussions to acquire Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE), a manufacturer of optical components used in telecommunications networks and AI data centers. Wall Street initially reacted negatively, as Marvell stock declined more than 8% following reports of the discussions.

Story Continues

The concerns are understandable. At the end of its fiscal second quarter, Marvell held approximately $3.9 billion in cash on its balance sheet. Lumentum boasts a market capitalization of $84 billion, meaning that an acquisition of this magnitude would require substantial borrowing, additional share issuance, or some combination of both by Marvell.

Even so, I see the strategic rationale here. One challenge facing AI data centers is moving information quickly and efficiently between large clusters of processors. Copper-based connections have limitations around bandwidth, distance, and power consumption. But optical interconnects offer an attractive alternative.

Lumentum specializes in lasers and optical components that support these systems. By integrating Lumentum's technology with its networking and custom silicon portfolio, Marvell could offer customers a more comprehensive suite of AI infrastructure solutions.

On a deeper level, acquiring Lumentum would build on Marvell's purchase of Celestial AI, a photonics company specializing in optical connectivity. In the long run, these investments could help Marvell become a critical supplier across multiple layers of the AI infrastructure stack.

Can Marvell become a trillion-dollar company?

Huang's prediction might sound ambitious at first glance, but Marvell's long-term financial projections help explain his enthusiasm. During its investor day earlier this month, Marvell's management outlined a path to reach between $70 billion and $90 billion in annual revenue by fiscal 2031, which largely corresponds to calendar 2030. At the midpoint, this implies $80 billion in annual sales.

For perspective, Marvell generated $8.2 billion in revenue during fiscal 2026. Reaching management's midpoint forecast would represent a tenfold increase over just five years!

The company believes this growth could support roughly $30 in adjusted earnings per share (EPS) by fiscal 2031. If Marvell achieves this target and is able to command a price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 30, its stock would trade around $900 per share. That translates into an implied market capitalization of roughly $810 billion, or roughly 309% upside from today's price action.

This analysis is simply here to illustrate that Marvell offers compelling long-term prospects, regardless of whether it joins the trillion-dollar club. While Nvidia and AMD will remain important players in AI computing, Marvell's assembly of custom silicon, advanced networking, and optical connectivity could allow it to capture an increasingly valuable portion of the data center market.

For investors who can stomach some volatility as the AI infrastructure era enters a new phase, I see Marvell as one of the best AI semiconductor stocks to watch.
