Tom Sepenzis, Vice President of Investor Relations and Strategy. Please go ahead.

Tom Sepenzis: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Silicon Motion's third quarter 2026 financial results conference call and webcast. Joining me today is Wallace Kou, our President and CEO, and Jason Tsai, our CFO. Wallace will first provide a review of our key business developments, and then Jason will discuss our third quarter results and outlook. Following our prepared remarks, we will conclude with a Q&A session. Before we begin, I would like to remind you of our safe harbor policy, which was read at the start of this call. For a comprehensive overview of the risks involved in investing in our securities, please refer to our filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Story Continues

For more details on our financial results, please refer to our press release, which was filed on Form 6-K after the close of the market yesterday. This webcast will be available for replay in the investor relations section of our website for a limited time. To enhance investors' understanding of our ongoing economic performance, we will discuss non-GAAP information during this call. We use non-GAAP financial measures internally to evaluate and manage our operations. We have therefore chosen to provide this information to enable you to perform comparisons of our operating results in a manner consistent with how we analyze our own operating results.

The reconciliation of the GAAP to non-GAAP financial data can be found in our earnings release issued yesterday. We ask that you review it in conjunction with this call. With that, I will turn the call over to Wallace.

Wallace Kou: Thank you, Tom. Hello. Thank you for joining us to the call today. I am pleased to report that we delivered another quarter of strong growth with revenue of $560 million and gross margin of 53.7%, driven by the growth in Ferri for automotive, Edge AI, and boot drive storage, our Edge SSD business, and our emerging MonTitan controller for enterprise SSD. We drove another quarter of higher operation performance, delivering the second consecutive quarter of record earnings per ADS, as we continue to capitalize on our product and market diversification strategy. We are on track to deliver record revenue in 2026 with over 100% top-line growth.

Our strategy is simple, deliver real value to customers and focus where we are uniquely differentiated so we can generate strong ROI for shareholders. For our edge controllers, we have become the de facto standard for mobile, IoT, and PC controller solutions. For NAND makers and virtually every module maker with outsourcing become a much more meaningful portion of the market. Our matched controller technology and design expertise deliver solutions that are better performing, consume less power, and are more cost-efficient than either in-house or other merchant solutions. Our strong share gains are driving significant growth despite end market weakness, and we expect this to continue.

Our MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers are winning across the ecosystem with leading NAND makers, hyperscalers, and CSPs, and with the module makers that supply AI server to hyperscale and enterprise customers. Our success is based on our unique combination of two decades of controller and firmware design experience and our history of managing more NAND than anyone in the industry. This has created an incredible, solid foundation for our leading enterprise controller products. We expect our MonTitan revenue ramp to accelerate as we introduce our next generation PCIe 6 controller next year. Lastly, for our storage solution segment, our strategy has always been to focus in areas that are underserved by NAND makers.

We are rapidly growing share in this vital low density, smaller volume market that require more design and customization work. We have spent more than a decade building one of the industry's broadest automotive-grade portfolio, supported by dedicated quality and supporting team. Today, that foundation positions us to capture fast-growing compute and storage demand across cars, drones, and increasingly robotics. For our enterprise boot drive solution, our unique combination of broad controller platforms, best-in-class firmware, technical know-how, NAND suppliers relationship, and manufacturing capability put us in an ideal position to serve the growing need of AI infrastructure market.

As a result, we are rapidly evolving to much more balanced and profitable company as a new enterprise in AI product enhance our leading consumer controller share, strengthening our competitive position from AI infrastructure to the edge to deliver long-term sustainable revenue and earning growth. I would like to take a moment to address the current market environment. The AI super cycle has driven robust demand of HBM, DRAM, NAND, HDDs for the past several quarters, with no sign of slowing down. Prices have risen sharply over the past year and the strained substrate supply across memory and storage enterprise market remain relatively insensitive to price.

PC, smartphone, and other consumer device OEM are struggling to bring affordable product to market, given today's memory and storage cost, and the consumer unit volume are declining as a result. We expect conditions to stay difficult until bit supply come back into balance with demand. New NAND fabs are planned for 2028, and NAND makers continue to add bit through higher layer count. We do not see this changing the current supply-demand imbalance to any great degree. Flash makers continue to prioritize enterprise and high-capacity solution, creating new and expanding opportunity for Silicon Motion. Our growth is benefiting from more outsourcing and larger opportunity in enterprise and the storage solution market that we are uniquely positioned to win.

We are at the beginning of the journey in the enterprise and AI market, and our early success will drive accelerating demand for our next generation storage technologies. Let me now detail our embedded eMMC and UFS business, which include controller for smartphone IoT connected devices. Our eMMC, UFS business was up over 100% year-over-year in the first half of 2026 as the NAND makers are shifting their resources toward DRAM and HBM solutions, allowing module makers to take share in the mobile market. This has helped drive our market share gains as module makers look to third-party controller partner to make their mobile solution.

In the third quarter, eMMC and UFS revenue declines modestly from the prior quarter, reflecting customer launch timing and the challenging smartphone OEM face in offering affordable device amid the higher NAND and DRAM prices. We expect the headwind to persist in the near to mid terms, until additionally memory and storage supply comes online. Across the markets that we sell our eMMC, UFS controller, OEM are reducing specification to try to offset the rising memory and storage cost.

We expect our eMMC, UFS business to remain relatively flat in the near term given the current market challenging, but I do believe we can return to growth next year and beyond as our new UFS 4.1 controller and UFS 5 controller ramp and driving higher ASPs. Now turning to our SSD controller business, which include Edge and MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers. This business delivers strong sequential and year-over-year growth. In Edge SSD, our PCIe 5 investment continue to pay off, with growth in both our four-channel and eight-channel controllers. PCIe 5 currently represent approximately 10% of the PC market, and we expect this will grow to 20%-25% of market by the end of 2027.

Providing a strong runway for further growth. Our leading position in PCIe 5 is driving greater market share gains within the PC market. As the industry transition from PCIe 4 to PCIe 5, we expect to see further top-line improvement given the higher ASP associated with these next-generation products. We are currently working with all the major NAND makers and most of the leading module makers to deliver compelling SSD solutions that leverage PCIe 4 and PCIe 5 controllers. We are tracking well ahead of expectation to achieve our market share goals of 40% through Apple by 2028, and believe we will continue to improve our position.

While PC unit headwinds associated with the higher memory and storage prices present challenges, we believe we will drive further top-line growth through the market share gains and ASP increases as the market shift to PCIe 5 continues. I would now like to provide you with an update on our new MonTitan enterprise SSD business. NAND remains a critically important technology across enterprise and AI storage ecosystem, and MonTitan is positioned for rapid growth in the coming years. This eSSD solution delivers high speed, low latency storage that targets compute and data storage application for enterprise AI platforms. Our first two customers began shipping TLC eSSD for compute that leverage our MonTitan controller in the second quarter.

All seven of our announced customers are on track to begin commercial ramp in 2026 with both TLC-based compute and QLC-based data storage products. TLC-based compute eSSD using MonTitan are expected to grow more quickly than QLC-based data storage eSSD in the near term, until greater supply of 2 terabit die become available. Encouragingly, four of our six NAND makers have started production of 2 terabit QLC die to date, and we expect all NAND makers to begin shipping 2 terabit QLC by end of 2027. Momentum will accelerate through next year.

During the third quarter, we taped out our next-generation 4nm PCIe 6 MonTitan controller targeting hyperscalers and CSPs, and expect to begin sampling in the first quarter of 2027. We have one design with multiple tier one customers, including NAND flash makers, hyperscalers, and CSPs. The new controller was designed for both compute application using TLC and data storage using QLC NAND as a performance shaping and multi-tenancy service architecture extremely well suited for a Gen AI infrastructure. We continue to see increased inbound interest in our MonTitan controllers, and expect this new enterprise controller segment will help us deliver long-term sustainable top and bottom-line growth.

Finally, I would like to provide an update on our Ferri automotive, edge, and enterprise boot drive storage business. Our solution business, which includes Ferri and boot drives, delivered the strongest result in the third quarter, with revenue up over 75% sequentially, representing over 40% of our revenue. Our automotive business has been a particularly strong source of strength, delivering better than expected top-line results and higher gross margins. We continue to scale this business quickly as we know automotive market, its customers, and the supply chain extremely well, which has driven significant backlog for long-term growth as we accelerate our share gains. We have since spent more than a decade developing our automotive products and certifications.

Today, our storage controller and firmware offer the broadest portfolio of solution to serve every part of the automotive market. Our success in automotive has drawn interest in Ferri for other large growing markets, including robotics, drones, and advanced networking. In the emerging robotic market, we are actively engaged with several companies that want to use our storage product. We are seeing multiple opportunities in humanoid robots and other physical AI systems, including vision, lidar, and compute storage. Our early conversation suggests robotic opportunity may be larger than automotive, and we believe Ferri is ideally suited to address it. Our fast-growing boot drive business is also gaining momentum.

We estimate that the market will be approximately $3 billion in 2026, growing to over $5 billion by 2030. In the third quarter, we won design with several new Tier one customers for networking and AI infrastructure products. These programs are expected to ramp over the next two years and will substantially improve our backlog visibility. As the average capacity of enterprise boot drives is much smaller than compute and data storage SSD drives, the NAND makers no longer prioritize this market. Additionally, our DRAMless controller delivers the performance, reliability, endurance this drive needs with lower power consumption requirements, smaller form factor, and the lower cost than DRAM-based design.

Boot drive handles the operation system, logging, and system management rather than heavy data workload, so they do not need the expense of onboard DRAM for DPU, router, and switch products. As AI infrastructure builds out at large numbers of servers, the networking and DPU equipment shipments are increasing rapidly, each needing reliable boot storage, driving the growing demand for DRAMless boot drives. We have been the primary supplier for DRAMless boot drive controllers to the NAND maker that have historically served this market, but they are moving on the higher density opportunity.

Silicon Motion are uniquely positioned with the right technology, the right support, the leading security firmware, and proven ability to procure NAND, making us the best partner for those needing a boot drive solution. Looking ahead, however, we are seeing significant new opportunity for boot drive with onboard DRAM. Given the strong demand of AI inference and agentic AI, near CPU boot drive with DRAM provide lower latency and open compute project features that are in increasingly high demand. As the NAND maker have shifted resources toward HBM, DRAM, and higher capacity compute and data storage SSD, there is a growing shortage of near CPU boot drives with DRAM.

We estimate that this market will reach over $10 billion by 2030, making a significant new opportunity for Silicon Motion. We are already in discussion with multiple potential customers for boot drive that leverage our industry-leading eight-channel and PCIe 5 controller that can serve the near CPU market to further expand our market opportunity, and expect to begin ramping product for this market in the second half of 2027. Our Ferri automotive, edge AI, and boot drive solution business are performing especially exceptional well, and these are many large and growing opportunity for our product in this segment.

Our backlog has increased significantly in just the past three months, and we expect many additional customer design wins in automotive, edge AI, and boot drive solution to deliver significant future growth. We continue to benefit from our proven ability to secure NAND in a difficult environment from multiple NAND suppliers, and this continues to be a powerful differentiator for our company. In conclusion, Silicon Motion delivered its fourth consecutive quarter of record revenue as we executed across a rapidly diversifying business. We are a fundamentally stronger company today with a stronger balance sheet, broadest range of solution and product, and more opportunity ahead than at any time in our history.

Our broad portfolio serves surging AI demand from the data center to the edge. That breadth gives us balance across our market and the flexibility to seize growing opportunity while navigating challenge like those we face today in PC and smartphones. I am extremely proud of our teams. Together, we have built a durable, diversified business powered by best-in-class technology, expanding share and new end markets, strengthened by two decades of relationship with OEMs, module makers, and NAND makers. I am more confident than ever that we will continue to deliver broad-based, sustainable growth long term. Now let me turn the call to Jason to go over our financial performance and outlook.

Jason Tsai: Thank you, Wallace, and good morning to everyone joining us today. I will discuss additional details of our third quarter results and then provide our outlook. Please note that my comments today will focus primarily on our non-GAAP results, unless otherwise specifically noted. A reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP data is included with our earnings release issued yesterday. Before I get into the results, I would like to comment briefly on our convertible bond issuance on August 13th. We raised an aggregate $1.15 billion with net proceeds to the company of $1.127 billion. This successful raise was increased from the initial offering of $800 million.

This new CB at 0% interest and an initial conversion price of $380.50 represents a conversion premium of 65% over the last reported sale price of SIMO on August 10th, the day the deal was announced. This additional capital significantly strengthens our balance sheet and will help fuel our growth and enhance our working capital to scale our business. Now, turning to our results. We delivered an outstanding third quarter, surpassing our expectations, driven by stronger execution and demand trends. In the September quarter, sales increased 24% sequentially and 131% year-on-year to $560 million, coming in well above the high end of our guided range of $519 million-$541 million, delivering our fourth consecutive quarter of record revenue.

We experienced strong growth across most of our businesses in the third quarter, with standout growth in Ferri for automotive, enterprise boot drives, and SSD controllers, including Edge and MonTitan for enterprise. Gross margins of 53.7% was significantly better than guidance as we capitalize on new product introductions and benefited from better mix and better-than-expected margins in our Ferri automotive products. Operating expenses slightly decreased sequentially to $120.7 million and operating margin increased 32.1%, well exceeding our guidance, driven by higher-than-expected revenue and gross margin in the quarter. Earnings per ADS was $4.35, a 79% increase sequentially and a 333% increase compared to same quarter last year.

Total stock-based compensation, which we exclude from non-GAAP results, was $17.3 million in the September quarter. We had $953.6 million in cash equivalents, and restricted cash at the end of the third quarter, compared to $181.8 million at the end of the second quarter. Cash increased in the third quarter due to the successful $1.15 billion convertible notes offering that we executed in the quarter, offset by the increase in working capital, dividend payment, and the repayment of the short-term bank loan. Our strategy, as Wallace outlined at the start of this call, continues to drive growth and expand our opportunities.

Our experience, our customers and partners, and our unmatched technology and development of NAND controllers and solutions has driven a significant transformation of the company. While the NAND market continues to be dynamic, our investments across consumer, enterprise, data center, and AI applications are the foundation of our rapidly growing business. As a result, we believe the momentum in our business will continue in the fourth quarter and now expect revenue to grow 5%-10% sequentially to $588 million-$616 million, with growth across nearly all our product segments led by Ferri for automotive, enterprise boot drive solutions, and MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers.

We believe our SSD controller business will be flat to slightly down given the current memory and storage environment and typical seasonality. Gross margins are expected to increase sequentially to 54%-55% in the December quarter, given the continuing improvement in product mix. Operating margin is expected to grow to 36%-37% as continued strong revenue growth and higher profitability drives the leverage to the bottom line. Our effective tax rate is expected to be 20%, and stock-based comp and dispute-related expenses are expected to be in the range of $34.6 million-$35.6 million. 2026 is on track to deliver record revenue for Silicon Motion, with top line expected to more than double year-over-year.

While we continue to invest heavily in R&D this year to expand our portfolio of leading-edge solutions, we are confident that along with the higher revenue and improved gross profitability, our operating margins will exceed 30% exiting this year. We expect this momentum to carry into 2027. Our strong backlog across all of our businesses gives us confidence that we can grow revenue by at least 40% next year, with gross profitability to be in the low to mid 50% range. Our mix is improving. With more contribution from enterprise controllers and Ferri automotive solutions, we should be able to sustain this higher margin level.

It is also worth emphasizing that these new enterprise opportunities represent larger addressable markets than our consumer segments. Because they are greenfield opportunities for Silicon Motion, we can grow significantly by gaining share without depending on further market growth. Any market expansion would only add to our potential upside. We set out to diversify beyond consumer applications into automotive and enterprise, and that strategy is now producing outsized results. Our longstanding leadership in merchant controllers and our multiyear investments in enterprise and AI SSDs are beginning to bear fruit. The solutions we are winning in these markets offer far greater visibility, much longer product cycles, and significantly higher barriers to entry, which together underpin sustained growth in revenue and profitability.

As these wins ramp across a broad mix of end markets, consumer cycles will have less influence on our results. Our visibility is improving significantly, and our business will become meaningfully more resilient and predictable. Our balance sheet has never been stronger, and we are well-positioned to capitalize on the fundamental drivers at our foundation of the transformation that Wallace Kou spoke about earlier. I look forward to sharing more on our progress next quarter. This concludes our prepared comments. I would like to open up the questions now. Operator?

Operator: Our first question comes from the line of Neil Young of Needham & Company. Please ask your question, Neil. Your line is open.

Neil Young: Hey, good morning, guys. First question, just given that you just gave us the expecting revenue to grow by at least 40% next year and gross margin in the low 50% range, curious if you could sort of dive into maybe the main drivers of that. Given that gross margin, you expect sort of resetting the long-term target, it sounds like now. I would expect more of the growth to be driven by sort of the higher margin business like Ferri and MonTitan, but any comments that you can add further on to 2027? Thanks.

Jason Tsai: Yeah, I think that is right. I think we are seeing significant traction with MonTitan. We are seeing the automotive, Ferri for automotive, ramping very aggressively as well. A lot of these Ferri projects, especially in automotive, these are multi-year engagements where, once we are qualified in, we have got a really long-standing position with that socket, with that customer. We are working with virtually every automaker in the world for a variety of solutions going into a significant amount of their portfolio, but significant room for growth still.

So based upon our backlog, based upon the growth we anticipate from MonTitan, as well as other SSD controllers and Ferri for automotive, we believe that we can sustain these low to mid 50% gross margins.

Neil Young: Okay, great. That is helpful. Just in this quarter, bringing it back, looking at the Ferri and boot drive, obviously the growth continuing is really great. Could you, by any chance, give us some more detail? It sounds like Ferri might have outgrew boot drive in the quarter. Obviously, beyond automotive, I should say, in Ferri, curious to learn more about the robotics and where you guys play in that. Thanks.

Wallace Kou: I think because of Ferri for automotive been for a long time, so we see the custom base are very strong. For this year, definitely it is Ferri for automotive, it grows stronger. However, our boot drive also gaining momentum with the diversified customers, more than just GPU customer and our TPU customer. We recently winning all the networking and server customers. We see our enterprise boot drive will grow even much faster next year. Robotics, I think it is still very early stage, and the total volume is still very small, but we try to make sure we will be in when the market take a boom.

Jason Tsai: Keep in mind, a lot of the features within the Ferri for automotive products are the same features that the robotics requires, right? Which is high temp, vibration, all of the things that go into a car largely go into the robotics as well. So having that certification already, having those products already, puts us in a significant advantage to penetrate this market as it grows.

Neil Young: Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. We will now take our next question from the line of Craig Ellis of B. Riley Securities. Please ask your question, Craig, your line is open.

Craig Ellis: Yeah, thanks for taking the question, and team, congratulations on the tremendous momentum that it seems you have in the business. I wanted to start with a question for you, Wallace. Very exciting to hear about the engagement that you have got with Near CPU Boot drives, because the performance gains, given reduced latency with the way that can implement are really quite profound, and it seems like that could be a very significant market. The question is this: Do you see this implementing on more of a custom basis across customers, or is JEDEC going to move super quickly and get standards out here in another quarter or two?

Then, can you just talk a little more about how you would see the early part of the ramp for Silicon Motion?

Wallace Kou: Now we see opportunity come from the early third quarter, because conventionally, this Near CPU Boot drive with DRAM belong to NAND makers. Because all NAND makers are busy and try to produce at least eight terabyte, 16 terabyte Compute SSD. They have less interest of resource on NAND allocation for the low capacity Near CPU Boot drive. The Near CPU Boot drive primary density is about one terabyte, two terabyte, and some also 512 gigabyte. four terabytes, very, very few. I think because we can see it will be probably a very, very big gap of shortage supply for 2027. Many, many customers come to Silicon Motion.

We are preparing discussion, and I think the solution, definitely need to have a customized sum feature and tailored for individual server and leading hyperscalers. This is not a simple work. We will try to focus on select the NAND and make sure we follow the OCP requirement and provide the firmware. I think we will be ready for the firmware and solution by early Q1, and production ramp will be second half 2027.

Craig Ellis: That is really helpful. The second question is really a higher level question for you and Jason. The team has done a phenomenal job operationally this year, putting the business in a position to grow 100%+ year-on-year. Can you help us understand the positioning that you feel like you are in with wafer supply, packaging, et cetera, to support the 40% growth? If demand is greater, given some reports that things like agentic AI, CPUs could grow 47% next year, can you just help us understand if there is upside potential in the supply chain to meet greater demand than that 40%? Thank you.

Wallace Kou: As you know very well, in semiconductor industry today, everything is in shortage, right? From substrate, from material, from wafer, from NAND, from memory, from even test capacity. But I think our manufacturing operating team did a very good job. We secured our 2027 wafer with TSMC primarily. Also, we also secured the test capacity and assembly capacity and the substrate material. So we believe we are able to support our growth for 2027. Jason mentioned we see we definitely can grow minimum 40% year-over-year. I think in next quarter earning call, we will provide more meaningful guidance for our 2027.

Craig Ellis: Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. We will now take our next question from the line of Sebastien Naji of William Blair. Please go ahead, Sebastien. Your line is open.

Sebastien Naji: Yeah. Thank you, and good morning. Thanks for taking the questions, and congrats on another record quarter here. My first question is maybe a little bit higher level and strategic. As your SSD solution business continues to grow as a share of revenue hit over 40% in Q3, it is driving greater NAND pricing exposure into Silicon Motion's model. That is a little bit of a shift for a company that was largely tied to volume growth historically. So maybe just how do you think about managing this new pricing dynamic and how it could impact your growth and margins, particularly if NAND pricing starts to come down?

Wallace Kou: Yeah, you asked a very good question. I think we definitely manage the NAND price increase and negotiate with the customer to pass through the cost to customers, so we benefit from the sale revenue growth. We believe the NAND price increase will come to moderate because the spot price for module maker now has become challenging. We see the Q3, Q4 NAND pricing are rather similar. For next year, we also see the, although will be a single digit growth quarter, but it will be moderate. For our business, why we focus on automotive and boot drive, because the end customer want to have a long-term contract and support and supply.

Our contract with customers and price will stay with at least two quarter, and we negotiate price every six months. We are able to manage the price and the cost, and that is why we can see through the demand, and we can manage our gross margin continually. We see the NAND wafer price will be more stable in comparison last year.

Jason Tsai: One more thing, Sebastien. I think certainly there is a fear that, if NAND flash prices begin to come down, how does that affect our growth? I think one of the things that we are seeing in automotive, even in boot drives, is that there is some just despeccing going on. I think all things being equal, if NAND availability was better, if pricing was better, our customers would double their density or more in some cases.

I think between a combination of kind of respeccing to normal specs as well as additional opportunities, additional customers that is coming online over the next 12, 18, 24 months, I think we are well positioned to continue to grow even as the NAND market stabilizes over the next two years.

Sebastien Naji: Got it. Great. That's helpful. Maybe just as a related follow-up around the funding that you raised and the working capital needs, I just wanted to get maybe a better sense for your ability to continue funding all of your working capital and inventory build with the cash that you have on hand. Can you maybe just talk a little bit about how quickly you expect inventory, particularly around NAND, to flow through the model and what it would take to maybe potentially need further capital down the line?

Jason Tsai: Yeah. For us, we're targeting about two quarters turnaround time between when we get the NAND and when we generate the cash flow. So, our expectation is to be able to turn that inventory relatively quickly, and generate the cash flow to support ongoing growth of our business. But when we did the raise, we talked about the raise being sufficient to fund our working capital needs for the next couple of years, based upon today's expectations. Obviously, as the business continues to grow and hopefully as it exceeds expectations, we'll continue to reevaluate that. But that's, at least right now for our visibility, we believe we're in a good spot.

Sebastien Naji: Great. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. Our next question comes from the line of Suji desilva of Roth Capital. Please ask your question, Suji, your line is open.

Suji Desilva: Hi, Wallace. Hi, Jason. Hi, Tom. Congratulations on the progress here. The MonTitan product, the higher KV cache density you're expecting, are there innovations coming from HBM and DRAM that might offset the opportunity for SSDs and KV cache? I'd love to get your thoughts there. What's a good concept of the number of MonTitan and SSDs needed per GPU for KV cache?

Wallace Kou: I think the MonTitan demands from very wide range, not only from the AI server and for hyperscaler and also for the CSP, but also for NVIDIA ecosystem. I think we don't know the percentage how, but we see the demand for Compute SSD this year is bigger due to the NAND price is very expensive. But we also see the momentum for high capacity QLC coming for next year. I believe, when Samsung, Hynix, 2TB QLC can move to production, we'll see more QLC demand for data storage. MonTitan itself can handle both the Compute SSD and the Storage SSD.

For KV cache, particularly for CMX, for NVIDIA structure, I think they will redefine and try, because the price is very expensive, they try to reduce the minimum capacity for each of their route and trade. I think this will be probably, they will announce it early next year, and I think the related ecosystem will help him provide. I think as well as the CMX KV cache demand is growing, as well as demand additional eSSD. That's good for us, for MonTitan, because it increase our controller demand.

Suji Desilva: Okay. Thanks, Wallace. Very helpful. The other question's for Jason, perhaps. 40% plus revenue growth next year, you talked about an operating margin guide in the 30s. Just how are you managing the OpEx and R&D growth, given that you have so many different end markets and projects you're focusing on? What's a kind of a growth rate for OpEx versus revenue that would be kind of a framework for us to think about?

Jason Tsai: Yeah. We'll get into more specific guidance around 2027 in January. This year we taped out a number of 6nm and as well as four nano products. So, we're spending a lot of money on tape-out and design this year already. We anticipate continuing to invest next year. Again, we'll talk more about the specific OpEx guidance next year in January, but our expectation is that we will continue to be able to deliver operating margin leverage next year as well.

Suji Desilva: Okay. Thanks, Jason. Appreciate it. Thanks, guys.

Operator: Thank you. Our next question comes from the line of Mehdi Hosseini of Susquehanna International Group. Please go ahead, Mehdi, your line is open.

Mehdi Hosseini: Yes. Thanks for taking my question. A couple of follow-ups from me. Wallace, Jason, can you quantify what percentage of your total revenue were attributable to Ferri, boot drive, and PCIe SSD, and how each percentage would change into next year? I have a couple of follow-ups.

Wallace Kou: I would say we cannot party about detail, but about 40% our total revenue is around the solution from Boot Drive and Automotive, 60% from controller.

Mehdi Hosseini: Would those mixes change dramatically next year?

Wallace Kou: Next year, the solution Boot Drive Automotive might grow to 50%, but so far we didn't accurate, but I think that we see probably will be balanced next year, 50/50 between controller and solutions.

Mehdi Hosseini: Okay. Given how your exposure to the consumer end market is less looking forward compared to prior years, should I assume that there is no more seasonality from Q4 to Q1?

Jason Tsai: Again, Mehdi, we will get into more specific Q1 and 2027 guidance in January.

Mehdi Hosseini: I was hoping to get a preview. You mentioned you are more driven by enterprise, and I am just trying to, maybe qualitatively, you can help us to.

Jason Tsai: No, I can. Certainly, I think the enterprise becoming a bigger portion of the mix, Ferri becoming a bigger portion of the mix, I think certainly normal consumer seasonality will certainly be more muted going forward as consumer business becomes a smaller percentage of our business.

Mehdi Hosseini: Is there any update on arbitration? It would be great to tell us whether the key milestone and how we track into those.

Jason Tsai: Yeah. We did the closing arguments in Singapore arbitration in March, and we are still anxiously awaiting the results. We don't have any other updates at this point, but certainly once the results come out, we'll be talking about those things quite a bit. But right now, there's no additional comments we're making around the arbitration.

Mehdi Hosseini: Okay. Thank you.

Operator: Our next question comes from the line of Gokul Hariharan of J.P. Morgan. Please go ahead, your line is open.

Gokul Hariharan: Yeah, hi. Thank you very much. The first question is on the near CPU boot drive opportunity. Wallace, I think you said you will start your solutions in the second half of next year. Could you talk a little bit about how big that opportunity can scale into? Because your enterprise boot drive partnership with NVIDIA, it scaled up very rapidly. But could you talk a little bit about how the opportunity is and how fresh that opportunity is, given that there are already a fair number of incumbents there? I just wanted to understand, the TAM is big, but how quickly can you scale this business?

Wallace Kou: I think that 10, will be a minimum $10 billion by 2030, because the density is bigger than the DRAMless boot drive. Because the NAND maker did not pay attention, but this business belonged to a NAND maker in the past, because especially the three NAND maker have DRAM. But because all the NAND makers, they focus on high capacity compute SSD, and the data storage SSD. So there is lack of resource and attention in the near CPU boot drive with DRAM. So that's why the supply becomes shortage, and many tier one customer come to Silicon Motion. We see the great opportunity.

We also work with the leading NAND maker to see how we can work together to resolve the issue. So whether they will support more NAND. And, also we need to resolve manufacturing and also including some DRAM supply, too. But we believe we'll start to ramp in the second half of this year. We also work with some module maker partner, because they will use our controller in the firmware, but we will have a different business model to work with them to benefit some financial results. Anyway, this is a new opportunity, and we just really don't have enough R&D resources.

There's a great opportunity for Silicon Motion to grow, and they could grow even faster in 2028 and 2029. Because we have the great idea controller and fitting very well, and we have the firmware technology, and suddenly the controller, very lucky, have a certain OCP feature built in, so we don't need to redo the new ASIC. I think a lot of our NAND makers, they don't have a such controller today. So that's why we are in a great position to expand to the new market.

Gokul Hariharan: Got it. Just to follow up there. When you win business, do you have to win by individual server customer, or you just design into a chip platform and you kind of become the de facto in that chip platform, similar to what you do for the current enterprise boot drive?

Wallace Kou: All the near CPU boot drive today is M.2 form factor, 22 by 80.

Gokul Hariharan: Yes. Yeah.

Wallace Kou: They need a low power, because our controller, Silicon Motion controller, our SM8000A, is ideal to fitting very well. This controller needs just a DDR4, or LPDDR4. So well-positioned into fitting this searching. There is some NAND maker also want to work with us, but we have limited resources. We just have to make sure the firmware is ready. We will support two different NAND, by Q1 next year, and hopefully ramping smoothly in second half of next year.

Gokul Hariharan: As long as it is M.2 standard, you can start shipping. There is no additional qualification by individual server customer, et cetera, which takes time.

Wallace Kou: We are already working with our module maker, our customer, and they will support the leading tier one server maker. They may ship earlier by Q2 next year. It is only with support controller. Our own solution, total solution, will probably be ready shipping in second half next year.

Gokul Hariharan: Understood. Second question is for Jason. Jason, first on gross margins. Historically, we have seen Ferri and any NAND solution business operate in the probably lower than 40% or 40% kind of gross margin levels. Now, obviously, you have made a meaningful step up in gross margins for solution business as well. As NAND price starts to stabilize or not really go up a lot, how should we think about the margins? Are these the steady state margins that you expect the solution business to earn, given it is more enterprise related? Secondly, could you also talk a little bit about next year looks like, based on Wallace's comment, the SSD solutions business will grow faster than 40%?

What is the support that you need from an inventory perspective? Inventory already has gone up to about $800 million or so. Could you talk a little bit about how you think about how much working capital support you would need to support that kind of additional probably 50% plus growth in the solution business?

Jason Tsai: Yes. In terms of the gross margin question on the solutions business, as Wallace pointed out, we are negotiating six-month pricing contracts with our customers, and we expect to turn our inventory here within that period as well. Maintaining very tight controls around working capital and price protection and margin protection for our products and our P&L. We anticipate that, certainly with automotive, these are qualified products going into projects that are multi-year, three to five years in length. Pricing as well as supply agreements are agreed upon at the beginning of these engagements. We are confident that we can maintain better margins, especially as the solution complexity, the design, the support becomes more onerous.

Having the higher margin supports all of that. In terms of the working capital, as I said, with the raise that we have done, we are confident that we can support the next couple of years' worth of business based upon what current forecasts look like. We will continue to grow inventory, but obviously in anticipation of a 40%+ year, we have grown inventory now. We will continue to grow inventory in the next quarter, in the fourth quarter, and then we will start seeing obviously the turns of that inventory come back into cash flow as we progress.

Gokul Hariharan: Got it. Okay. Thank you.

Operator: Next question comes from the line of Daniel Yen of Morgan Stanley. Please ask your question, Daniel. Your line is open.

Daniel Yen: Yeah. Thanks, Wallace and Jason, to take my question, and congratulations on a great result. I want to switch gears to a very different question. Wallace, you just mentioned about some opportunities, for example, for your boot drive, for example, enterprise SSD. But I want to ask what will be your strategy right now in China. I think China is still the important region, and I think in China, we also have CSPs, we have NAND supplier, NAND makers. We also have a lot of module houses there. But at the same time, I think competition is still there.

So I want to consult you on Silicon Motion's strategy right now in China both with the NAND makers, with the competitors, and also how should we address maybe the future demand from the CSP in China.

Wallace Kou: Okay, you asked a very good question, Daniel. I think that we really want the balance between China and also the rest of world. China has YMTC, NAND maker, they are very strong. They grow very fast. We also support and collaborate with the YMTC directly or indirectly with the module maker. I think the enterprise portion, we see they will become stronger in 2027. I think we definitely work closely for China CSP for hyperscaler. Believe us, and I think that is why we try to grow China local R&D. Eventually, we want China, our local R&D can support China customer. In Taiwan, we support the rest of world, especially for U.S. customers.

Secondly, I think the China, they are growing enterprise controller company, but in the past, they also like to make enterprise C drive. In the past, as you know, NAND pricing is cyclical. They have a downside, they have upside. So some enterprise controller company, they buy the NAND in the downside, they are selling the drive in the upside. But nowadays, there is no longer the cyclical price going up or stable, right? So very hard for enterprise controller company, you use it converting to selling the whole solution if you do not win hyperscaler or even NAND maker of the CSP customer. So I think our strategy is very simple. We winning NAND maker business and designing directly.

We win hyperscaler customer in both U.S. and China. We also win CSP directly. But we do not make enterprise solution. We only sell controller and our firmware. We enable the module maker and the NAND maker. They sell and utilize our controller and the firmware, make enterprise solution, and selling to the customer. So this is where we are. That is why building Silicon Motion ecosystem, working together and supporting the growing opportunity in both China and U.S.

Daniel Yen: I see. Very clear. Wallace, if I may follow up, how should we think about the overall competitive landscape on a controller in China right now? Just want to get your opinion.

Wallace Kou: For enterprise, we really do not even. There is one or two basic company move to the IPO, but we do not see they are strong enough to compete in the long term, not just one technology or business model, right? I do not really see any threat from them. Even some also want to go overseas. Today, we feel pretty comfortable for our position and with our technology, and we have a very strong developing pipeline for both our PCIe Gen 5 as well as Gen 6.

Daniel Yen: I see. Yes. Thanks for this. The second question from me is that since right now I think you are issuing the convertible bond, I want to ask if there is any change on your dividend policy potentially in the future? Also I think just overall, how should we think about your capital structure going forward? Do you have a target, any ratio you are looking at? I think this question is actually coming from some of the investors who subscribe your convertible bond. Thank you.

Jason Tsai: Yeah. Dividend and capital allocation certainly continues to be a priority. We increased our dividend a couple of weeks ago from $2-$2.30 per ADS per year. We have had a history of increasing our dividend over the last 10 years or so, and our expectation is that we can continue to look at that strategically over time and continue to look at opportunities to raise that. The three priorities for us on capital return is dividend, share buybacks opportunistically, and then M&A as it makes sense, and that is unchanged. But certainly right now, working capital needs continue to increase as well.

The CB raise puts us in a much better position to drive growth in our business with better working capital as well.

Daniel Yen: Thank you, Jason. That is all my questions. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. We have now reached the end of the question and answer session. I will now turn the conference back to Mr. Wallace Kou for closing comments.

Wallace Kou: Thank you everyone for joining us today and for your continuing interest in Silicon Motion. We will be attending several investor conferences over the next few months. The schedule of these events will be posted on the investor relationship section of our corporate website, and we look forward to speaking with you at these events. Goodbye for now.

Operator: Thank you for your participation in today's conference. This does conclude the program. You may now disconnect your lines.

news.Title: Why Marvell Stock Is Down Today
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) stock is sinking, down 13.9% as of 2:44 p.m. ET on Thursday, Oct. 29, after a report said the chipmaker is close to buying a big optics supplier.

The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite were down 0.7% and 1.7%, respectively.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Marvell has its eye on Lumentum

Bloomberg reported after Wednesday's close that Marvell is in advanced talks to acquire Lumentum , a company that builds key optical components for AI data centers. An announcement could land as early as next week according to the report, but nothing has been finalized.

Marvell can't just write a check

Marvell has about $3.93 billion in cash and equivalents, and given Lumentum's $83 billion market cap, Bloomberg has reported it is likely to be all stock. That means dilution for existing shareholders. The company actually acquired a smaller optics company last year, in a $3.5 billion deal that included $1 billion in cash. This would be substantially larger.

The price tag is the real question

Marvell's overall business is humming, with Q2 revenue up 37% to a record $2.74 billion. I think optics is a smart place for Marvell to grow, but this is a massive deal relative to its size, and whether it pays off is a question we can't really answer until more details come to light.

news.Title: MRVL Stock Sinks as Marvell Technology Reportedly Considers Acquiring Lumentum
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (MRVL) shares opened notably lower on Thursday following reports that the chipmaker is in advanced talks to acquire optical-components specialist Lumentum (LITE). An agreement could emerge as soon as next week, with the transaction set to meaningfully expand MRVL's exposure to the technology connecting artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.

Despite today's dip, however, Marvell stock is trading at more than 1.5x its price at the start of this year.

More News from Barchart

Dear AMD Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendar for November 3

Dear Chevron Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 30

Elon Musk Invests $1 Billion in Skydance Stock. He Could Be Setting the Stage for a Major Starlink Deal.

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

What Triggered the Selloff in Marvell Stock Today

One explanation for today's decline in MRVL shares is the financing burden. Heading into Oct. 29, Lumentum had a market cap of roughly $83 billion, compared with less than $4 billion in cash at the end of its latest reported quarter.

This means the custom AI chips specialist will likely have to issue new stock or tap the debt market to fund this transaction; the former will dilute existing investors and the latter will introduce interest costs. And it's fair to assume that successfully acquiring Lumentum will require Marvell to pay a meaningful premium, which would further raise the financial burden.

In short, strategic benefits alone are insufficient to establish that acquiring Lumentum would create value. Without a disclosed purchase price, funding structure, and synergy targets, shareholders can't yet determine whether the potential rewards justify the commitment.

Piper Sandler Recommends Buying MRVL Shares

Piper Sandler analysts nonetheless reiterated their "Overweight" rating on Marvell shares today, with a $400 price target indicating significant upside potential. The investment firm highlighted optical networking's growing importance in accelerating AI data transfers while reducing power consumption, identifying Lumentum's high-powered lasers as an enabling technology.

The strategic opportunity is to address more of the connectivity demands created by increasingly powerful AI systems, analysts told clients, adding that the two companies already showcased complementary optical technologies earlier this year, targeting faster, more energy-efficient networks.

Story Continues

Barchart also currently holds a "40% BUY" average opinion on MRVL, indicating technical momentum is also in its favor for the near term.

Wall Street Remains Bullish on Marvell Technology

Other Wall Street firms seem to agree with Piper Sandler's bullish view on Marvell Technology as well. The consensus rating on MRVL stock sits at "Strong Buy," with the mean price target of about $337 indicating potential upside of more than 50% from here.

news.Title: Okta Surges 158% YTD: Should Investors Hold the Stock Now?
news.Content:
Okta OKTA shares have jumped 157.5% year to date (YTD), outperforming the broader Zacks Computer & Technology sector's return of 17.4%. The company is benefiting from growing demand for identity security, artificial intelligence (AI) agent governance, enterprise modernization and expanding adoption of its newer products. However, intense competition, uncertainty surrounding AI adoption, slowing customer growth and near-term revenue headwinds remain concerns. What should investors do with OKTA stock? Let's find out.

Okta Rides on Strong Enterprise Demand & New Products

Okta is well-positioned to benefit from increasing enterprise investments in identity security as organizations accelerate AI adoption and modernize their cybersecurity infrastructure. The proliferation of autonomous AI agents across applications, cloud platforms and enterprise systems is creating demand for identity discovery, authentication, access controls and governance. Okta for AI Agents enables enterprises to discover, secure and govern AI agents while enforcing access policies across heterogeneous environments. Growing adoption of agentic AI is expected to expand the company's addressable market and create additional cross-selling opportunities across its identity security portfolio.

Okta's newer offerings, including Okta Identity Governance, Okta Privileged Access, Identity Security Posture Management, Identity Threat Protection and Okta for AI Agents, are helping customers address increasingly complex security requirements. Deals involving newer products generated an average annual contract value (ACV) uplift of approximately 40%, highlighting significant cross-selling and upselling opportunities. Increasing adoption of these solutions is likely to strengthen Okta's competitive positioning, deepen customer relationships and support subscription revenue growth.

Okta is benefiting from solid demand among large enterprises, improving sales productivity and strong customer expansion activity. During the second quarter of fiscal 2027, the number of customers generating more than $1 million in ACV increased more than 20%, bringing the total to more than 600. Strong pipeline conversion and deal expansions contributed to record bookings for a quarter outside the fiscal fourth quarter. The company is strengthening collaborations with Anthropic, Amazon Web Services, Cisco, OpenAI, Databricks and Snowflake to expand identity controls across AI applications and enterprise systems.

Intense Competition & Moderating Revenue Growth Hurts OKTA

Story Continues

OKTA is facing stiff competition from the likes of Microsoft MSFT, CrowdStrike CRWD and Cisco Systems CSCO. YTD, CrowdStrike, Cisco and Microsoft have returned 114.6%, 42.2% and 9.4%, respectively.

OKTA Stock's Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Per OKTA management estimates, Microsoft's workforce access management market share is at approximately 40% compared with Okta's 30%. Competition is also intensifying as cybersecurity vendors, enterprise software providers and AI infrastructure companies expand into identity governance and AI agent security.

Okta continues to face challenges in accelerating overall revenue growth despite improving bookings and subscription demand. For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, the company expects revenues of $813-$817 million, indicating approximately 10% year-over-year growth. Current Remaining Performance Obligation growth is projected at 11-12%, below the 14% growth recorded in the second quarter. Okta expects fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 10-11%, including an approximately one-percentage-point headwind from shifting more professional services business to global system integrator partners.

news.Title: Arista Networks (ANET) vs. CSCO and AVGO: Is AI Data Center Expansion Creating a Long-Term Networking Winner?
news.Content:
Is ANET a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Arista Networks, Inc. on TradersPro's Substack. Since the thesis was published on August 29th, ANET shares have pulled back amid profit-taking and valuation concerns after a strong rally, creating a near-term pause while AI networking demand continues to support the longer-term growth case. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on ANET. Arista Networks, Inc.'s share was trading at $186.72 as of October 28th 2026. ANET's trailing and forward P/E were 55.91 and 33.82 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

This isn't the first time we see a networking equipment company pitched as a great investment. ANET shares gained 42.50% year to date. Comparable technology stocks like Cisco Systems and NVIDIA gained 43.18% and 15.49%, respectively, during the same period. Why are AI infrastructure stocks rising so much and is it really a good time to buy them?

In May, we published an article about the 10 Stocks That Will Make You Rich Over the Next Decade and ANET ranked #4 in that article. ANET returned 31.76% since then. So, hedge funds were right about ANET. This article highlights ANET among the 12 Best NYSE Stocks to Buy for Long-Term Investment. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Arista Networks, Inc. (NASDAQ:ANET) makes the networking equipment that connects servers, data centers, and enterprise systems, using high-speed switches, routers, and its EOS software. Its biggest growth opportunity right now is AI infrastructure, where massive AI computing clusters need faster, more reliable connections between chips, making Arista Networks, Inc. a key supplier of the "plumbing" behind the AI boom.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

The company is also benefiting from steady spending by large cloud providers, growing demand for office and campus networking, expansion into routers, and a large existing customer base that keeps generating repeat business. Investors are watching closely because AI infrastructure still can't keep up with AI demand, and that gap is where Arista Networks, Inc. sees its opportunity ( see how Arista's $6.9 billion in deferred revenue relates to its cash flow ).

The bullish argument is simple: as AI systems get more powerful, they need more bandwidth and faster connections. This lets Arista Networks, Inc. grow along two paths at once — more AI clusters being built overall, and each cluster needing better networking gear than the last. Its core switching business is well placed for this, while its newer push into routers and campus networks adds growth beyond just AI data centers.

Story Continues

A key part of the long-term story is the shift toward liquid-cooled AI infrastructure, which changes how high-density data centers are built. As AI servers use more power and generate more heat, traditional cooling starts to fall short, forcing new approaches to layout, power delivery, and system design. If this shift continues, Arista Networks, Inc. could play a bigger role in connecting these next-generation systems, though it still has to prove it can turn this opportunity into consistent growth.

The main risk is a slowdown in AI spending or delays in data center buildouts by large customers. Networking demand depends heavily on this spending, and factors like component shortages, tariffs, power limits, and the sheer complexity of liquid-cooled builds could all slow things down. The market already expects a lot from Arista Networks, Inc., so continuing to win AI networking deals matters more than ever — any stumble in adoption of its newer platforms could weigh on the stock.

Another risk for the stock is that AI networking growth benefits competing technologies more than Arista's Ethernet platforms. Rising spending on AI clusters does not guarantee that customers will choose Arista's equipment. Its annual report identifies InfiniBand and NVLink as competing technologies, often sold alongside NVIDIA's graphics processors as integrated solutions. Customers choosing these packages could leave less networking business available to independent suppliers. Arista might then need to offer lower prices or spend more on development to win deployments. That would put pressure on margins even if overall AI infrastructure investment remains strong. In our opinion, the stock's premium becomes harder to justify if the networking market expands faster than Arista's ability to capture profitable orders.

Beyond AI, growth in campus networking, routing products, and support revenue from its installed base gives the company other ways to grow, so it isn't fully dependent on one market. Still, how fast AI-related demand keeps growing will be the biggest factor in whether the stock's current optimism is justified.

The stock's momentum has picked up recently, with trading volume rising and the stock moving into a stronger technical position — a sign of growing investor confidence. But the longer-term outlook still hinges on whether AI spending keeps converting into real networking orders, and whether growth holds up as expectations climb. A slowdown in AI infrastructure spending or delays from big customers could pressure the stock even if the broader industry keeps growing.

AI remains the main reason investors are bullish, but there's a risk that demand stays concentrated among just a handful of large cloud customers. If those customers keep expanding their AI clusters and adopting newer, denser computing setups, Arista Networks, Inc. should keep benefiting. The real test is whether this turns into lasting earnings growth rather than a short-term spending wave.

Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed but generally constructive signal. As per our database, 91 hedge fund portfolios held Arista Networks, Inc. at the end of the second quarter, up from 85 in the previous quarter. This increase suggests institutional interest in the stock strengthened, supporting its appeal as an AI infrastructure investment. By comparison, Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) was held by 101 hedge funds, up from 97, NVIDIA was held by 285 hedge funds, up from 275, and Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) was held by 170 hedge funds, down from 173. NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) stood out with the strongest increase in hedge fund interest by number of funds, followed by Arista Networks and Cisco Systems, while Broadcom saw a modest pullback, suggesting institutional enthusiasm remained broadly positive across the group.

Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture for Arista Networks, Inc. relative to its peers. About 1.17% of Arista Networks, Inc.'s float is sold short, almost identical to Broadcom Inc. at 1.14%, but below NVIDIA Corporation at 1.30% and Cisco Systems, Inc. at 1.53%. This suggests Arista Networks, Inc. is drawing similarly limited skepticism to Broadcom Inc., with bearish bets remaining low across all four AI infrastructure companies.

Valuation Analysis

ANET's forward P/E is 33.82x. Broadcom Inc., Cisco Systems, Inc., and NVIDIA Corporation trade at forward P/Es of 18.25x, 20.53x, and 13.79x, respectively. ANET's own forward P/E was 32.75x on December 31, 2025, making its current multiple approximately 3% higher. We believe the current valuation reflects strong investor expectations for AI networking demand, continued cloud spending, and expansion into campus networking and routing. However, the premium appears demanding despite Arista's strong profitability and earnings growth, as its multiple exceeds all three peers. Arista's revenue increased 37.7% to $3.04 billion in the second quarter of 2026, while net income rose approximately 36% to $1.21 billion, demonstrating that increased demand is translating into substantial earnings. We believe ANET can justify its current valuation without accelerating beyond this growth rate if strong earnings growth persists and margins remain resilient. If Arista maintains its Ethernet leadership and successfully converts AI investment into sustained earnings growth, its premium could remain justified, but we would wait for a lower entry price given the limited room for disappointment.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Arista Networks Inc (ANET) by Charly AI in April 2025, which highlighted the AI and cloud networking growth, strong margins, balance sheet strength, and long-term upside despite near-term pressures. ANET's stock price has appreciated by approximately 168.66% since our coverage. We believe ANET could offer an attractive entry point at a lower valuation if AI networking demand sustains earnings growth and Arista preserves its margins, despite its premium multiple and competition from integrated alternatives.

Arista Networks is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds . While ANET could offer long-term upside if it converts AI networking demand into sustained earnings growth, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential at more attractive valuations, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than ANET and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock .

news.Title: 3 Stocks to Consider From a Flourishing Networking Industry
news.Content:
The Zacks Computer - Networking industry participants are expected to benefit from the networking infrastructure upgrade driven by AI workloads, cloud computing, big data, network security and next-generation connectivity.

The proliferation of AI workloads and hyperscale data centers is accelerating investments in high-speed interconnects, optical networking and Ethernet switches. Players in this space are focused on capitalizing on the multi-billion-dollar AI infrastructure opportunity. Increasing adoption of AI-driven applications across enterprises is also driving investments in next-gen networking infrastructure capable of supporting higher bandwidth, lower latency and heightened security requirements. Continued deployment of 5G, the proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT), industrial automation and edge computing is strengthening demand for reliable connectivity solutions. Increasing deployment of Wi-Fi 7 also presents a significant growth opportunity.

Also, the explosion of AI workloads requires a major upgrade to observability infrastructure. There is a greater need for continuous monitoring of hybrid environments and tighter security amid rising attacks. This will spur demand for innovative networking products, favoring prospects for prominent industry players such as Cisco Systems CSCO, Digi International DGII and Lantronix LTRX.

However, cautious IT spending amid heightened uncertainty over global macroeconomic conditions and volatile supply-chain dynamics due to tariff troubles continues to be concerning for the participants in the near term. Fierce competition is an overhang on pricing power and margin expansion.

Industry Description

The Zacks Computer-Networking industry comprises companies that offer networking and Internet-connected products, including wireless (Wi-Fi and Long-Term Evolution or LTE), Ethernet and powerline, focusing on dependability and ease of use. The products are available in numerous configurations to cater to the changing requirements of consumers in each geographic territory where it operates. Several industry players also provide mission-critical IoT solutions and network security services to help clients build next-generation connected products, and implement and manage critical communications infrastructures in demanding environments with enhanced safety levels. Focus on developing IoT sensors, drones and wearables amid increasing demand for cloud computing-based contact tracing applications is driving the industry.

Story Continues

4 Trends Influencing the Industry's Future

Technological Advancement Opening Business Avenues: The proliferation of generative AI, agentic AI and high adoption of cloud and data-intensive applications is driving higher traffic and creating a need for advanced optical networking, high-speed interconnects, Ethernet switches, routing and wireless infrastructure. The transition toward 800G and 1.6T networking technologies is expected to further drive infrastructure modernization and capacity expansion.

Expansion of industrial IoT and edge computing, and the increasing popularity of smart connected devices are further creating growth opportunities. Rising cybersecurity concerns are emerging as a key tailwind, driving demand for solutions such as threat detection, network monitoring and zero-trust security architectures.

Continued Deployment of 5G to Boost Growth Prospects: The continued expansion of the 5G technology hinges on substantial investments to upgrade infrastructure in the core fiber backhaul network to support growth in data services. Efforts to develop smart connected homes, hospitals, factories, buildings, cities and self-driving vehicles bode well for industry players. These firms invest heavily in LTE, broadband and fiber to provide additional capacity and improve Internet and wireless networks. These initiatives hold promise.

Wi-Fi 7 Upgrade Cycle to Drive Momentum: Brisk technological advancement, dynamic products, high-speed connectivity, low latency and evolving industry standards define the networking industry. The growing clout of the latest Wi-Fi 6E-compliant residential gateways, Wi-Fi routers, set-top boxes and wireless range extenders is a testament to the same. The increasing demand for connecting more devices to the network has been driving demand for Wi-Fi 6E devices. Wi-Fi 6E addresses Wi-Fi spectrum shortage issues by providing continuous channel bandwidth to support a higher number of connected devices without compromising speed. The rollout of Wi-Fi 7 bodes well for the companies in this space.

Macroeconomic Turmoil Is Concerning: Global macroeconomic weakness and volatile supply-chain dynamics are persistent concerns. Tariff troubles, especially between the United States and China, remain an overhang on global supply chains. Inflation could affect spending across small and medium-sized businesses globally and uncertainty in business visibility could dent the industry's near-term performance.

The computer networking industry remains highly competitive, with a large number of established and new players vying for market share. As growth stabilizes, competition often intensifies, leading to pricing pressure and margin compression.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Bright Near-Term Prospects

The Zacks Computer-Networking Industry is housed within the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. The industry carries a Zacks Industry Rank #75, positioning it in the top 30% of more than 247 Zacks industries.

The group's Zacks Industry Rank, which is the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates bright near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than two to one.

Before we present a few stocks you may want to consider for your portfolio, considering bright prospects, let us look at the industry's recent stock-market performance and valuation picture

Cisco Systems: Headquartered in San Jose, CA, the company offers identity and access, advanced threat and unified threat management solutions.

Cisco is benefiting from the demand for AI Infrastructure solutions, with hyperscaler demand acting as a key catalyst. The company expects AI infrastructure revenues from hyperscalers to reach $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027.

On the last earnings call, CSCO noted that accelerating agentic AI is driving a "networking super cycle" resulting in increasing demand for its Networking stack to support inferencing across cloud, on-premise and edge environments. In October, Cisco announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to develop an open industry specification for next-generation 400G-per-lane pluggable optics, further strengthening its position in the evolving AI networking ecosystem.
