news.Title: TYL Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on SaaS Growth and Margin Expansion
news.Content:
Tyler Technologies, Inc. TYL reported third-quarter 2026 non-GAAP earnings of $3.52 per share, which increased 18.5% year over year and beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 2.03%.

Tyler Technologies' revenues increased 8.7% year over year to $647.6 million but missed the consensus mark by 0.55%. The performance was supported by strong SaaS demand, transaction revenue growth and improved operating efficiency. Annualized recurring revenue (ARR) increased 11% to $2.28 billion, highlighting the strength of Tyler's recurring revenue model.

TYL's Recurring Revenue Base Strengthens in Q3

Recurring revenues increased 11% year over year to $568.8 million and accounted for 87.8% of total revenues. Excluding the impact of the Texas payments contract, recurring revenues grew 12.8%, reflecting healthy underlying demand.

Subscription revenues rose 15.3% to $462.6 million, supported by continued cloud adoption and transaction growth. Maintenance revenues declined 4.6% to $106.2 million as on-premises customers continued migrating to SaaS offerings.

Tyler Technologies, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Tyler Technologies, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Tyler Technologies, Inc. Quote

Tyler's SaaS Momentum Drives Subscription Growth

SaaS revenues jumped 21.2% year over year to $242.2 million, reflecting sustained demand for cloud-based government solutions. Transaction revenues increased 9.5% to $220.4 million despite the discontinuation of revenues under the Texas payments contract in the fourth quarter of 2025.

Excluding the Texas contract impact, transaction revenues grew 14.2%, subscription revenues increased 17.8%, and total revenues rose 10.2%. These adjusted growth rates highlight the strength of Tyler's underlying business.

Management also highlighted progress in cloud modernization. Wasco County, OR, became the first Enterprise ERP customer to go live on Tyler's multi-tenant Cloud Living platform, with broader rollouts targeted for 2027.

TYL's Bookings Growth Signals Healthy Public Sector Demand

Total bookings increased 7.3% year over year to $646 million. Total SaaS bookings grew 14% to approximately $262 million in total contract value, supported by new contracts, customer expansions, renewals and cloud migrations.

New SaaS deals contributed approximately $22 million in annual contract value, while on-premises migrations added $18.6 million. Total SaaS ARR added 32.1% to approximately $40.6 million.

Management highlighted healthy government budgets, robust request-for-proposal activity and strong sales demonstrations. New SaaS annual contract value bookings increased 75%, underscoring customer demand for digital modernization.

Story Continues

Tyler's AI Adoption Expands Across Government Agencies

Tyler continued advancing its government-focused artificial intelligence strategy, closing approximately 300 deals containing AI solutions year to date, including roughly 130 during the third quarter.

The company made 11 AI agents and assistants generally available and expects to expand AI functionality to 25 agents by year-end. Its Resident AI Assistant now supports deployments across 11 states.

Notable wins included Nebraska's statewide Resident AI Assistant deployment and multiple contracts for AI-powered Priority Based Budgeting. These developments reflect growing opportunities to commercialize AI across Tyler's existing government customer base.

TYL Expands Profitability on Favorable Revenue Mix

Non-GAAP operating income increased 14.8% year over year to $182.1 million, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded 150 basis points to 28.1%. The improvement reflected a favorable shift toward higher-margin SaaS and transaction revenues, cloud efficiencies and disciplined expense management.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 13.4% to $192.7 million. GAAP operating income rose 19.5% to $117 million, while GAAP operating margin improved to 18.1% from 16.4% a year earlier.

Research and development expenses increased to $63.3 million from $51.8 million, reflecting continued investment in product development and innovation.

Tyler Generates Record Quarterly Free Cash Flow

Cash flows from operations increased 10.7% year over year to $282.5 million. Free cash flow rose 11.9% to a quarterly record of $277 million, supported by earnings growth and improved working capital performance.

Free cash flow margin expanded to 42.8% from 41.5% in the prior-year quarter, demonstrating improved cash generation.

Tyler ended the quarter with approximately $905 million in cash and investments and $1.4 billion in debt.

The company repurchased approximately 1.1 million shares for $379 million during the quarter. Year-to-date repurchases represented approximately 8.5% of outstanding shares, with roughly $1.37 billion remaining under its authorization.

TYL Provides Updated 2026 Earnings and Revenue Outlook

For full-year 2026, Tyler expects revenues between $2.535 billion and $2.565 billion. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 revenues is pegged at $2.55 billion, within management's projected range.

news.Title: Lumentum stock rises on report of possible merger with Marvell
news.Content:
What happened: Marvell Technology ( MRVL ) stock dropped 12% on Thursday on reports that the AI chipmaker is in advanced talks to purchase optical parts maker Lumentum ( LITE ). Shares of Lumentum surged as much as 5% before trimming gains.

What's behind the move: The potential multibillion-dollar mega deal between the semiconductor designer and Lumentum was first reported by Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter.

An agreement could be announced as soon as next week. Lumentum has a market value of about $83 billion, compared with Marvell's roughly $221 billion.

What else you need to know: The acquisition would give Marvell greater access to optical technologies and manufacturing capacity, which have become critical bottlenecks of the AI infrastructure build-out.

Lumentum makes lasers and other optical components as increasingly powerful AI systems require faster connections. Marvell, which competes with Broadcom ( AVGO ), designs high-speed infrastructure and custom chips that enable AI computers to communicate with one another.

Earlier this year, Marvell stock rallied sharply after AI chip heavyweight Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang described the chip designer as "the next trillion-dollar company.

The company joined the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) index in June. Marvell shares are up more than 190% year to date. Lumentum shares have rallied 140%.

news.Title: Prediction: Marvell Stock Will Be Worth This Much by 2030
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) is becoming one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI infrastructure boom, thanks to growing demand for its data center products. If the company delivers on its ambitious growth targets, the stock has plenty of room to run higher through 2030.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But before you consider adding it to your portfolio, it's important to understand what's driving that growth today.

Custom chips are making Marvell a bigger AI spending winner

One of Marvell's growth engines is its custom silicon business. That's because tech companies are increasingly shifting toward using AI data center processors designed specifically for their workloads rather than pricier GPUs with greater flexibility.

Developing these application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) requires strong engineering capabilities, intellectual property, and close collaboration with customers. Marvell has spent years building those capabilities, positioning itself to benefit as hyperscalers deploy more custom AI hardware.

The company's latest earnings show the opportunity is already driving significant growth. In the second quarter of its fiscal 2027, Marvell generated a record $2.7 billion in revenue, up 37% year over year. Its data center business grew 46%, driven by strong demand for AI-related products spanning connectivity, custom chips, and storage.

Marvell is already shipping custom silicon to the four largest U.S. hyperscalers, and these relationships create more opportunities for future design wins. Still, the biggest risk is that delays, cancellations, or changes in customer spending could significantly affect revenue growth. Competition from other semiconductor companies and from customers developing more of their own chips could also pressure margins.

Regardless, in conjunction with the earnings report, management raised its revenue outlooks for fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028, citing exceptionally strong AI bookings and accelerating demand across its data center portfolio. The company expects around $12 billion in revenue for fiscal 2027 and $20 billion for fiscal 2028. Those are huge jumps from the $8.2 billion in revenue it generated in 2026.

But Marvell isn't relying on a single product line to drive those gains.

A broader product lineup gives Marvell more ways to win

Story Continues

Marvell's expanding portfolio gives it several ways to benefit as cloud providers build more complex AI infrastructure. That breadth matters because the AI build-out cycle is creating opportunities in areas well beyond chips.

The company's "XPU attach" products are particularly interesting. As AI systems become more advanced, they require more components for networking, memory, storage, and security. Marvell can supply these components in addition to the customer's primary chips.

Management also identified interconnect technology as one of its more promising growth opportunities. That's because as AI systems become ever more complex, they need more powerful and higher-bandwidth technology to move data efficiently between chips and servers.

Management's long-term plan targets $37.5 billion in interconnect revenue alone, at the midpoint, in its fiscal 2031.

On top of that, Marvell has been investing in technologies designed to support optical connections. Its acquisition of Celestial AI, completed in February, expanded its capabilities in photonic interconnect technology for next-generation AI data centers.

With that, management estimates the company's total addressable market will reach around $400 billion by 2030. Its opportunities span custom silicon, interconnect, and storage, allowing Marvell to benefit from several layers of the AI boom.

Marvell has a compelling growth story which raises a big question: What might the stock actually be worth by 2030?

Three earnings scenarios show where Marvell stock could land by 2030

Marvell's custom chips and high-speed networking products give it multiple avenues for growth, and Wall Street is bullish. Among 39 analysts covering the stock, 30 rate it a strong buy, three call it a buy, and six rate it a hold. Their average 12-month price target on the stock is $337, and the highest target price is $450.

That said, a single target doesn't tell the whole story. In a recent investor day presentation, management laid out a long-term target of more than $31 in annual earnings per share (EPS).

Here's how that could play out: In a pessimistic case, custom chip programs could slip, and the company's EPS could dip to roughly $13. If the stock traded at 18 times earnings, it would be worth about $234, which is about where it trades today.

Meanwhile, a base case assumes that Marvell will deliver about two-thirds of management's target, or $20 in EPS. Trading at 22 times earnings, shares would be worth around $440, roughly 88% higher than today's price.

On the optimistic end, we can imagine Marvell hitting the $30 EPS target and the market paying 26 times earnings for the stock, which would price it near $780.

In sum, custom-chip ramp-ups and margins will likely determine what Marvell is worth by 2030, but which outcome we get will depend heavily on execution, too. Shares have swung between about $71 and $330 over the past year, so investors should be prepared for a bumpy ride.

news.Title: Silicon Motion (SIMO) Is Considered a Good Investment by Brokers: Is That True?
news.Content:
The recommendations of Wall Street analysts are often relied on by investors when deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock. Media reports about these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts changing their ratings often affect a stock's price. Do they really matter, though?

Let's take a look at what these Wall Street heavyweights have to say about Silicon Motion (SIMO) before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage.

Silicon Motion currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.25, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 12 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.25 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 12 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 10 are Strong Buy and one is Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 83.3% and 8.3% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for SIMO

Check price target & stock forecast for Silicon Motion here>>>

While the ABR calls for buying Silicon Motion, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential.

Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations.

This means that the interests of these institutions are not always aligned with those of retail investors, giving little insight into the direction of a stock's future price movement. It would therefore be best to use this information to validate your own analysis or a tool that has proven to be highly effective at predicting stock price movements.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

Zacks Rank Should Not Be Confused With ABR

In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures.

Story Continues

news.Title: What STMicroelectronics (STM) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in STMicroelectronics N.V.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Strong third-quarter performance: STMicroelectronics reported $3.76 billion in revenue, above the midpoint of its outlook, with non-U.S. GAAP EPS of $0.37. Industrial revenue rose 40% year over year, while communication equipment and computer peripherals surged 64%, driven by AI data centers and low-earth-orbit satellites.

AI and satellite demand are accelerating: ST expects about $1.3 billion in AI data-center revenue in 2026 and projects data-center revenue to more than double in 2027. Satellite communications revenue is also expected to reach or exceed 2026's record level, with capacity potentially limiting growth.

Positive outlook and margin plans: The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $4.15 billion at the midpoint and expects approximately $14.5 billion in full-year 2026 revenue. Manufacturing restructuring is expected to deliver more than 400 basis points of structural gross-margin improvement by late 2027 or early 2028.

Apple, Meta, and SpaceX Are Driving a Device Boom—These 3 Stocks Could Benefit

STMicroelectronics (NYSE:STM) reported third-quarter 2026 revenue above the midpoint of its outlook, citing strengthening demand across industrial markets and continued growth in artificial intelligence data centers and low-earth-orbit satellite communications.

Revenue totaled $3.76 billion, with gross margin of 37.3% and non-U.S. GAAP diluted earnings per share of $0.37. Chief Executive Officer Jean-Marc Chery said revenue outperformance was driven principally by communication equipment and computer peripherals, including AI data-center and satellite-related products, as well as communications and personal electronics.

→ Apple's Foldable iPhone Sold Out in Minutes, But Wall Street Has Questions

Industrial Chips Are in Rally Mode—5 Ways to Play

The company generated $351 million in free cash flow during the quarter. Inventory increased modestly to support expected fourth-quarter revenue growth, while distributor inventory declined and remained below STMicroelectronics' standard target, management said.

Demand, bookings and end-market performance

Chery said the recovery in the company's served markets continued to gain momentum in the third quarter. Sequential bookings increased and the overall book-to-bill ratio remained "well above two," with ratios above one across all end markets. Communication equipment and computer peripherals, as well as industrial, each had book-to-bill ratios well above three, according to management.

Story Continues

→ Coca-Cola Stock Is Everything AI Isn't—And That's Its Biggest Strength

STMicronelectronics Sends Industrial Chips Into Overdrive

The company's backlog stood at more than $20 billion at the end of the quarter, representing roughly five quarters of revenue at the midpoint of its fourth-quarter guidance. Chery said this level of backlog provided "appropriate visibility" for operations, although it remained below the peaks seen in 2022 and 2023.

Automotive: Revenue was flat sequentially and rose 5% year over year. ST cited demand for application-specific ICs and sensors used in core automotive systems, electric powertrains and advanced driver-assistance systems.

Industrial: Revenue increased 12% sequentially and 40% from a year earlier, supported by general-purpose microcontrollers, analog products and power-conversion devices.

Personal electronics: Revenue rose 12% sequentially but declined 4% year over year. Management said the stronger-than-expected third quarter did not reflect a customer pull-in.

Communication equipment and computer peripherals: Revenue climbed 14% sequentially and 64% year over year, primarily reflecting AI data-center and low-earth-orbit satellite communications demand.

By reportable segment, year-over-year revenue rose 8.8% in Analog Products, MEMS and Sensors; 11.3% in Power and Discrete Products; 24.1% in Embedded Processing; and 46.2% in RF & Optical Communications.

AI data-center and satellite growth drivers

→ Off-Price, High-Yield: Why Ross Stores Is Defying the Retail Slump

Management said AI data-center products remain a major company-specific growth driver. STMicroelectronics expects approximately $1.3 billion in AI data-center revenue during 2026, with more than 85% coming from RF-related products, including microcontrollers, silicon photonics and electronic ICs based on BiCMOS technology.

Chery said the company expects data-center revenue to more than double in 2027, with further growth anticipated in 2028. Rémy El-Ouazzane, president of the company's Microcontrollers, Digital ICs and RF Products Group, said microcontroller revenue in data centers is expected to double year over year in 2027. He added that silicon photonics is expected to become a meaningful portion of revenue next year, while BiCMOS contributions should become more visible in 2028.

El-Ouazzane said ST plans to increase silicon-photonics capacity by more than four times year over year, describing customer electro-optical yields as strong. In low-earth-orbit satellite communications, he said 2027 revenue should be at least as high as, and potentially higher than, the record level expected in 2026. The business could be constrained by capacity rather than demand, he said.

Margins and manufacturing restructuring

Third-quarter gross profit was $1.40 billion, up 32.2% year over year. Gross margin improved 410 basis points from a year earlier and 250 basis points sequentially, aided by lower unused-capacity charges and a better product mix.

However, third-quarter gross margin included roughly 60 basis points of unused-capacity charges and 40 basis points of nonrecurring costs tied to the company's manufacturing reshaping program. CFO Lorenzo Grandi said the company remains committed to an intermediate gross-margin model of 44% to 46% after completing the manufacturing transition.

The company expects more than 400 basis points of structural gross-margin improvement from reshaping its manufacturing footprint. Grandi said the benefit is expected to emerge toward the end of 2027 or in early 2028, subject in part to customer qualification timing as ST closes four legacy fabs and transfers production to newer facilities.

ST reported third-quarter operating income of $367 million, including $55 million in impairment, restructuring and related phase-out costs, plus $7 million in purchase-price-allocation effects from the acquisition of NXP's MEMS sensor business. Non-U.S. GAAP operating income was $429 million, representing an 11.4% margin.

Fourth-quarter and full-year outlook

For the fourth quarter, STMicroelectronics forecast revenue of $4.15 billion at the midpoint, plus or minus 350 basis points. That would represent sequential growth of 10.5% and year-over-year growth of 24.7%. The company expects gross margin of about 39%, plus or minus 200 basis points, including approximately 40 basis points of unused-capacity charges.

The outlook excludes potential effects from further changes in global trade tariffs. At the midpoint of its fourth-quarter outlook, ST expects full-year 2026 revenue of about $14.5 billion, up 22.8% year over year, with gross margin of roughly 36.4% and non-U.S. GAAP gross margin of approximately 36.6%.

Management also said it was comfortable delivering at least current consensus estimates for first-quarter 2027 revenue and gross margin, despite the quarter having 86 calendar days. The company expects 2027 operating expenses to rise, though Grandi said the increase should be accompanied by an improved expense-to-sales ratio as savings programs and lower startup costs partly offset investment in new opportunities and wage inflation.

Separately, Chery said the supervisory board requested that he be reappointed for an additional year as chairman of the managing board, president and CEO, subject to shareholder approval at the 2027 annual meeting. ST also announced organizational changes effective Jan. 1, 2027, including the appointment of El-Ouazzane as chief technology officer and Marco Cassis as chief strategic officer.

About STMicroelectronics (NYSE:STM)

STMicroelectronics N.V. (NYSE: STM) is a global semiconductor company that designs, develops, manufactures and markets a broad range of integrated circuits and other semiconductor products. Its offerings support applications in automotive, industrial, personal electronics, communications equipment and computer systems.

The company's product portfolio includes microcontrollers, analog and power semiconductors, sensors, microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), connectivity products and automotive chips.

news.Title: 聯電法說變法會「股價打跌停」 智原連拉2漲停
news.Content:
聯電（2303）28日公布第3季財報，營收創單季歷史次高、晶圓出貨量刷新紀錄，還預告2027年平均售價有望成長約10％，並追加32億美元，要布局先進封裝與矽光子。怎料「法說變法會」29日股價開低走低，股價一度打跌停。另一方面，集團旗下智原（3035）股價延續強勢，連拉2根漲停。

第3季營收742億元

聯電第3季合併營收達742.4億元，季增8％、年增25.6％，創單季歷史次高；毛利率34％，營業利益186.4億元，季增24.7％，歸屬母公司淨利164.3億元，每股純益（EPS）1.32元。第3季晶圓出貨量季增7.3％，突破120萬片12吋約當晶圓，創下歷史新高，產能利用率也從第2季的85％提升至92％，部分12吋晶圓廠產能已滿載，8吋晶圓廠營運亦明顯復甦。

展望第4季，聯電預估晶圓出貨量季增1％至3％，美元計價平均售價維持穩健，毛利率約34％，產能利用率則可望維持在91％至93％。執行長王石指出，高階智慧手機、工業應用需求強勁，車用市場也持續復甦，但電腦市場需求相對疲軟。隨著AI基礎建設持續發展，電源管理晶片（PMIC）、現場可程式化邏輯陣列（FPGA）及連接應用需求可望成長。

明年ASP喊漲1成

聯電看好2027年晶圓代工定價環境改善，預期平均售價將較2026年成長約10％，並從明年第1季開始呈現正向成長。然而，財務長劉啟東坦言，晶圓報價調升不代表毛利率就能同步大幅改善，因為原物料成本也在增加，加上未來數年折舊費用將持續上升，預期2027年折舊費用至少呈低個位數成長，2028年增幅可能進一步擴大。

聯電指出，未來至少3年，折舊與原物料成本都將對毛利率形成壓力，即使平均售價上漲，毛利率仍不容易回到過去景氣高峰水準。這也成為市場評估聯電後續獲利的重要變數，投資人關注漲價效益能否抵銷成本增加，以及產能受限後，營收與獲利還能有多少成長空間。

聯電重挫、智原連2根漲停

儘管營運展望不乏亮點，聯電股價仍遭賣壓襲擊。29日盤中最低殺到跌停價115.5元。相較之下，集團旗下智原受惠明年AI營收可望大幅成長，以及成功接獲美系雲端AI應用之大型專案，採用2奈米GAA製程，股價延續強勢，已連續第2個交易日攻上漲停，來到231.5元。

news.Title: Vicor Stock is Overvalued at 16.52X EV/Sales: Should You Still Buy it?
news.Content:
Vicor VICR shares are overvalued, as suggested by a Value Score of F. In terms of the trailing 12-month EV/Sales, VICR is trading at 16.52X, higher than the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's 8.19X. The company is trading at a higher multiple compared with peers, including Analog Devices ' ADI 15.17X and Texas Instruments ' TXN 13.82X, but cheaper than Monolithic Power Systems ' MPWR 17.76X.

Vicor's Shares Trade at a Premium

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Is Vicor worth buying at current prices? Let us dig deep to find out.

VICR Shares Ride on AI Prospects

Year to date (YTD), Vicor shares have outperformed the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector, as well as Monolithic Power Systems, Analog Devices and Texas Instruments. Vicor returned a whopping 93.4% YTD while the broader sector, Monolithic Power Systems, Analog Devices and Texas Instruments have returned 14.9%, 33.7%, 54.3% and 78%, respectively.

Vicor Stock's Price Performance

Vicor is benefiting from increasing demand for high-density power delivery solutions as AI processors require greater power efficiency and higher current density. The company's second-generation Vertical Power Delivery (VPD) technology is emerging as a key growth catalyst. VICR claims that its proprietary all-FPA technology can reduce AI processor power losses by 10-15%, while delivering more than 40 times the current gain of integrated voltage regulators (IVRs) and three times the current density of conventional voltage regulators. These advantages are expected to strengthen Vicor's competitive position as next-generation AI processors become increasingly power-intensive.

The company's expanding royalty business has been a key catalyst. In the third quarter of 2026, royalty revenues surged to $66.6 million from $21.7 million in the year-ago quarter. Vicor secured its first VPD license with a leading AI original equipment manufacturer and received licensing inquiries from two hyperscalers. The company expects royalty revenues of at least $43 million in the fourth quarter, even without additional licensing agreements. Further adoption of its patented technologies could create a growing, high-margin revenue stream, although quarterly royalty collections may remain uneven.

Manufacturing expansion represents another important long-term catalyst for the company. Vicor has acquired two additional sites for ChiP Fab-2 and ChiP Fab-3, potentially increasing total manufacturing capacity to nearly five times that of Fab-1. Initial equipment deployment at Fab-2 is expected in the second quarter of 2027. This expansion should help address production bottlenecks, support rising customer demand and unlock additional revenue opportunities.

Story Continues

VICR Benefits From Strong ATE Business & Balance Sheet

Vicor's growth opportunities also extend beyond AI processors. Strong demand for automatic test equipment (ATE) used in ASIC and memory testing is supporting the company's business, with leading ATE customers generating more than $100 million in annual revenues. VICR is also witnessing opportunities in industrial, aerospace and defense markets, particularly from emerging companies developing autonomous technologies. These diversified growth drivers should reduce dependence on any single application and support sustained demand for the company's power solutions.

Vicor's strong balance sheet further supports its long-term expansion plans. The company ended September 2026 with $513.1 million in cash and cash equivalents. VICR expects to finance Fab-2 and eventually Fab-3 without raising additional capital. Improving operating cash generation and increased production scale should strengthen the company' ability to fund innovation, expand manufacturing and capitalize on emerging growth opportunities.

Vicor's 2026 Earnings Estimate Revision Shows Rising Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings is pegged at $3.94 per share, up 8% over the past 30 days, suggesting 51% growth from the 2025 reported figure.

Vicor Corporation Price and Consensus

Vicor Corporation price-consensus-chart | Vicor Corporation Quote

The consensus mark for fourth-quarter 2026 earnings is pegged at $1.13 per share, down by four cents over the past 30 days and indicating 12% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Conclusion

Despite its premium valuation and impressive YTD rally, Vicor remains an attractive investment proposition, supported by strong AI-driven demand, expanding royalty revenues and growing adoption of second-generation VPD technology. The company's manufacturing expansion, solid backlog and strong balance sheet further strengthen its long-term growth prospects. Although elevated valuation and near-term capacity constraints remain concerns, VICR's technological leadership and expanding growth opportunities justify its premium and make the stock worth considering for long-term investors.

Vicor currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Lumentum Shares Jump 135% YTD: Can AI Momentum Sustain the Rally?
news.Content:
Lumentum LITE shares have surged 135% year to date (YTD), outperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's return of 16.5%. The outperformance reflects investor optimism about the company's expanding role in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, accelerating demand for optical connectivity and improving profitability. Strong hyperscaler spending, growing adoption of 1.6T optical transceivers, optical circuit switches (OCS) and next-generation laser technologies are strengthening Lumentum's growth prospects.

These factors have helped LITE shares outperform peers, including Cisco Systems CSCO, Broadcom AVGO, and Coherent COHR YTD. Shares of Coherent and Cisco have returned 27.8% and 45.3%, respectively, while Broadcom shares have dropped 1.1%. Despite robust demand, LITE faces challenges in expanding manufacturing capacity sufficiently to meet customer requirements. Apart from stiff competition, LITE's dependence on a limited number of major customers exposes its business to changes in purchasing patterns and capital spending priorities. So, what should investors do with the LITE stock? Let's find out.

LITE Stock's Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Lumentum Shares Are Overvalued

Lumentum shares are overvalued, as suggested by a Value Score of F.

In terms of the trailing 12-month price/sales, LITE is trading at 10.48X, higher than the broader sector's 5.57X. Lumentum is trading at a higher multiple compared with peers, including Coherent's 3.9X, Cisco's 6X and Broadcom's 9.39X.

LITE's Valuation

LITE Faces Multiple Challenges

Lumentum faces challenges in expanding manufacturing capacity sufficiently to meet customer requirements. Tight availability of laser components and other materials could restrict shipments and delay revenue realization. The company is expanding ultra-high-power laser production across its San Jose, U.K. and Greensboro facilities.

The company suffers from customer concentration. LITE's dependence on a limited number of major customers exposes its business to changes in purchasing patterns and capital spending priorities. Lumentum's two largest end customers accounted for 26.6% and 15% of fiscal 2026 revenues, respectively, representing a combined 41.6%. Moreover, the company's expanding OCS business currently depends heavily on one major customer.

Lumentum faces competition from established optical technology suppliers, including Coherent, Broadcom, InnoLight and Eoptolink. Additionally, the shift toward silicon photonics presents challenges for Lumentum's EML business.

Story Continues

Can Strong AI Opportunity Aid LITE's Prospects?

Lumentum is benefiting from increasing investments in AI data centers, which require high-bandwidth, low-latency optical connectivity. The transition from copper-based connections to optical technologies is creating opportunities across scale-out, scale-across and scale-up networking architectures. Increasing adoption of AI accelerators and larger computing clusters is driving demand for Lumentum's lasers, optical components and transceivers.

The company is benefiting from accelerating adoption of next-generation 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers as hyperscalers upgrade their AI networking infrastructure. Lumentum achieved record 800G shipments and initiated production shipments of 1.6T transceivers during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Lumentum expects the adoption of 1.6T transceivers to accelerate through calendar 2027, supported by deployments of custom AI clusters among leading hyperscale customers.

Lumentum's OCS business represents a significant growth opportunity as hyperscalers seek energy-efficient networking solutions. OCS technology enables dynamic traffic routing while reducing power consumption and optical signal losses compared with conventional electrical switching. OCS shipments doubled sequentially in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, while the company's first-quarter outlook included its first quarter of more than $100 million in OCS revenues.

LITE's 2027 Earnings Estimate Revision Shows Rising Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $21.40 per share, up 0.5% over the past 30 days, suggesting 146.8% growth from the fiscal 2026 reported figure.

Lumentum Holdings Inc. Price and Consensus

Lumentum Holdings Inc. price-consensus-chart | Lumentum Holdings Inc. Quote

The consensus mark for first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $4.22 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days and indicating 283.64% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Conclusion

Lumentum's strong exposure to AI infrastructure, accelerating adoption of 1.6T optical transceivers and expanding OCS opportunities bode well for its long-term growth prospects. Upward earnings estimate revisions further reinforce optimism. However, the stock's premium valuation, customer concentration, intense competition and manufacturing capacity constraints warrant caution. Following the sharp YTD rally, much of the growth potential appears priced in, limiting near-term upside. Hence, investors may consider holding LITE shares at current levels rather than chasing the rally, while monitoring execution and profitability improvements.

Lumentum currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Garmin Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Rise Y/Y
news.Content:
Garmin Ltd. GRMN reported pro forma earnings of $2.76 per share for the third quarter of 2026, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.38 by 15.97%. The bottom line increased 39% year over year from $1.99 reported in the year-ago quarter.

Net sales rose 12% to $1.99 billion and came in line with the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Fitness and Outdoor together accounted for 65% of sales, supported by demand for wearables and adventure watches. Gross margin expanded 420 basis points to 63.3%.

GRMN's Fitness Revenues Rise on Wearable Demand

Fitness revenues advanced 16% year over year to $694.3 million. The segment benefited from continued demand for wearables, with operating income increasing 19% to $230.6 million. Gross and operating margins were 63% and 33%, respectively.

During the quarter, Garmin launched the CIRQA Smart Band, a screenless wearable offering health and fitness insights. The company also recently introduced new Edge cycling computers, including the Edge 1060 with hands-free voice controls and the Edge Explore 3 series.

Garmin Ltd. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Garmin Ltd. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Garmin Ltd. Quote

Garmin's Outdoor Sales Surge on Adventure Watches

Outdoor revenues jumped 20% to $597.3 million, primarily driven by demand for adventure watches. Operating income climbed 37% to $233 million, while gross and operating margins reached 68% and 39%, respectively.

The company launched the f??nix 9 and f??nix 9 Pro adventure watch series during the quarter. It also introduced Garmin Drive GPS navigators featuring high-resolution ultrawide displays. The launches expanded Garmin's flagship adventure watch and navigation offerings.

GRMN Sees Growth Across Aviation and Marine

Aviation revenues increased 5% to $252.7 million, led by original equipment manufacturer product categories. Operating income rose 8% to $65.8 million. The segment recorded gross and operating margins of 78% and 26%, respectively.

Garmin unveiled the G2000 PRIME flight deck for high-performance piston and electric aircraft and announced certification of an all-glass retrofit cockpit for the original Cessna CitationJet.

Marine revenues grew 16% to $309.9 million, driven by broad-based demand led by sonar products. Marine operating income surged 90% to $94 million, while gross and operating margins were 64% and 30%, respectively. The company launched LiveScope 2 and received six Product of Excellence awards from the National Marine Electronics Association.

Garmin's Auto OEM Revenues Contract

Story Continues

Auto OEM revenues declined 20% year over year to $131.9 million, primarily due to domain controllers. The segment recorded a gross margin of 16% and an operating loss of $11.9 million compared with a loss of $16.7 million a year earlier.

Lower operating expenses helped narrow the operating loss despite the decline in sales. Garmin continues to work toward the launch of its Mercedes-Benz domain controller program.

Garmin's Operating Profitability Improves

Gross profit increased 20% year over year to $1.26 billion, while gross margin expanded 420 basis points to 63.3%. Operating income rose 34% to $611.6 million, with operating margin expanding 500 basis points to 30.8%. Favorable segment mix, lower product costs and approximately $33 million in refunds of previously paid tariffs supported profitability. GAAP earnings jumped 35% to $2.80 per share.

Operating expenses increased 10% to $646.1 million. Research and development expenses rose 9% to $312.9 million, mainly due to personnel costs. Selling, general and administrative expenses climbed 10% to $333.2 million, reflecting higher personnel-related and advertising expenses.

Garmin Returns Cash to Shareholders

Garmin generated $393.9 million in operating cash flow and $293.3 million in free cash flow during the quarter compared with $485.6 million and $425.1 million, respectively, a year earlier. Capital expenditures totaled $100.6 million. In the first three quarters of 2026, it generated operating and free cash flows of $1.33 billion and $1.04 billion, respectively. It incurred capital expenditure of $295 million during the first nine months of 2026.

The company paid $202 million in dividends and repurchased $41 million of shares. In the first three quarters of 2026, Garmin paid $578.5 million in dividends and bought shares worth $123.2 million. Approximately $407 million remained under its share repurchase authorization at the end of the third quarter. It ended the quarter with approximately $4.1 billion in cash and marketable securities and $2.25 billion in inventory.

Garmin Raises 2026 Outlook

Garmin now expects 2026 revenues of approximately $8.15 billion, up from its prior projection of $8.05 billion. Pro forma earnings are forecast at $10.80 per share compared with the previous outlook of $10.

The company raised its gross margin forecast to 61% from 59.7% and its operating margin estimate to 29% from 27%. The projected pro forma tax rate remains unchanged at 16.5%.

Management raised its 2026 guidance following record operating results and continued momentum heading into the holiday selling season.

GRMN's Zacks Rank and Stocks to Consider

news.Title: TXN's Gross Margin Crosses 64% in Q3: Can It Improve Further?
news.Content:
Texas Instruments Incorporated TXN delivered a strong improvement in profitability in the third quarter of 2026, raising hopes that its gross margin can climb further. The semiconductor maker reported a gross margin of 64.2%, up from 57.4% in the year-ago quarter and 61.4% in the previous quarter.

Texas Instruments' third-quarter gross profit rose 43% year over year to $3.89 billion, outpacing the 28% increase in revenues to $6.06 billion. Higher sales volumes supported the improvement, while better factory utilization, pricing and product mix also helped. These trends suggest that stronger demand can translate into better profitability when production facilities operate more efficiently.

Growth across key markets offers additional support. Industrial revenues increased more than 40% year over year, while automotive revenues grew at a mid-teens rate. Data center revenues surged about 95%, reflecting rising demand for chips used in expanding computing infrastructure. Continued strength in these markets could help TXN maintain higher production levels and spread manufacturing costs across more units.

Texas Instruments' 300-millimeter wafer manufacturing strategy could also support cost efficiency as output rises. Per the company, an unpackaged chip built on 300-millimeter wafers costs approximately 40% less than one built on 200-millimeter wafers. Texas Instruments has available cleanroom capacity in its Richardson, Sherman and Lehi facilities. Management plans to install additional equipment according to demand, supporting dependable supply and cost efficiency as production volumes increase.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for revenues and earnings indicates year-over-year growth of 37.7% and 94.5%, respectively. These projections imply continued business activity, which could further expand Texas Instruments' margins.

How Do TXN's Competitors Compare on Gross Margin?

Analog Devices, Inc. ADI is a close competitor in analog chips and signal-processing technology. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, ADI's revenues rose 40% year over year to $4.02 billion, while its GAAP gross margin increased to 67.3% from 62.1% in the year-ago quarter.

Its adjusted gross margin reached 72.5% from 69.2% in the year-ago quarter, highlighting strong profitability. These results put Analog Devices ahead of TXN's 64.2% gross margin.

Microchip Technology Incorporated MCHP is another competitor, supplying microcontrollers and embedded-control chips. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, revenues grew 38% year over year to $1.49 billion.

Story Continues

Microchip Technology's GAAP gross margin improved to 63.2% from 53.6% in the year-ago quarter, while its non-GAAP gross margin reached 63.8% from 54.3%. Higher factory utilization and recovering demand supported the improvement.

Both companies show how stronger demand and manufacturing efficiency can lift margins. Analog Devices' higher reported margin sets a competitive benchmark, while Microchip Technology's performance highlights the benefits of better factory utilization.

Shares of Texas Instruments have surged 78.1% year to date compared with the Zacks Semiconductor - General industry's 22.6% growth.

news.Title: HPE Benefits From AI Infrastructure Demand: What's Ahead?
news.Content:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE is benefiting from demand for artificial intelligence (AI) workloads across Agentic AI, Enterprise AI, Private Cloud AI, AI fabs and hyperscalers, leading to multiyear revenue growth and record backlogs.

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, HPE's Cloud & AI revenues reached $9 billion, up 25% year over year, with a 17% operating margin. Server revenues rose 35%, while traditional server orders increased 75% as customers favored AI-ready configurations and higher-value systems. HPE's fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 Cloud & AI revenues are expected to grow 60% to 72%.

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, AI systems orders were $2.4 billion, up more than 30% sequentially, while AI systems backlog rose 14% sequentially to $6.8 billion. Private Cloud AI orders increased triple digits year over year, showing wider adoption of HPE's on-premises AI factory approach.

HPE was also awarded a $3.5 billion inferencing deal with a hyperscaler customer, adding evidence that enterprise AI deployments are moving beyond pilots. Supporting its AI infrastructure, Hewlett Packard Enterprise is expanding its hybrid cloud operating model through GreenLake, which lets customers manage infrastructure and software across on-premises and cloud environments with consumption-based economics.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise has used acquisitions to add networking, cloud management, security and data-management capabilities around its hybrid IT model. These factors will support HPE's capabilities and long-term growth outlook.

How Competitors Fare Against HPE

Hewlett Packard Enterprise's closest competitors in this domain are Dell Technologies DELL and Cisco CSCO. Dell AI Factory combined with NVIDIA is arguably the most direct alternative for HPE private cloud AI.

Dell provides pre-integrated GPU servers, storage, networking and software for enterprise AI and competes head-to-head with HPE for Fortune 1000 AI deployments. Cisco focuses on AI networking and integrated AI Pods. Cisco has started competing strongly with HPE after acquiring Splunk and through its partnership with NVIDIA.

HPE's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise have skyrocketed 152.3% year to date, outperforming the Zacks Computer - Integrated Systems industry and the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's appreciation of 109.9% and 16.6%, respectively.

news.Title: FFIV Q4 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Systems Growth
news.Content:
F5, Inc. FFIV reported better-than-expected fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results. Non-GAAP earnings of $4.42 per share increased 0.7% year over year and surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.3%.

Revenues rose 13% year over year to $917 million, beating the consensus mark by 3.7%. Results benefited from robust systems demand, software expansion and hybrid multicloud adoption. Product revenues advanced 23%, marking the ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.

FFIV's Q4 Revenue Details

Product revenues, representing 56% of total revenues, increased 23% year over year to $510 million. Systems revenues jumped 29% to $239 million, driven by infrastructure refreshes, capacity expansion, competitive displacements and investments in digital sovereignty and AI readiness.

Software revenues rose 19% to $271 million. Subscription-based software revenues increased 16% to $229 million, representing 85% of software revenues. Perpetual license revenues climbed 37% to $42 million. Services revenues, accounting for 44% of total revenues, grew 3% to $408 million.

F5, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

F5, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | F5, Inc. Quote

Recurring revenue sources contributed 68% of quarterly revenues. Geographically, EMEA led growth with a 31% increase, representing 30% of total revenue. APAC revenues rose 14%, contributing 17%, while Americas revenues increased 5%, accounting for 53%.

F5 Benefits From Hybrid Multicloud and AI Demand

Management highlighted sustained demand from hybrid multicloud adoption, application security modernization and AI inference workloads. Platform consolidation remained a key opportunity, with 29% of F5's top 1,000 customers adopting three or more product families, up from 22% in fiscal 2025.

During the quarter, a large North American financial institution selected F5 for an eight-figure application delivery and security deployment, displacing four incumbent vendors. An Asian central bank technology authority also selected F5 for a national financial services cloud, replacing two competitors.

AI-related opportunities accelerated. Direct AI use-case bookings exceeded $100 million in fiscal 2026, growing nearly 300% year over year. The customer base for these solutions expanded fourfold to more than 200, supported by demand for AI data delivery, runtime security and AI factory load balancing.

FFIV Expands Security and Software Opportunities

F5 continued expanding its AI-powered security portfolio as enterprises sought protection against increasingly sophisticated application and API threats. Its AI-powered Distributed Cloud WAF capabilities attracted more than 300 customers since their March launch, with over 75% operating in blocking mode.

Story Continues

The company also gained more than 200 F5 Insight customers since its March launch. The platform provides automated fleet management and upgrade orchestration, helping enterprises reduce operational complexity and accelerate security updates.

For fiscal 2026, software revenues increased 8% to $870 million. SaaS and managed services annualized recurring revenues reached $211 million, up 14% year over year. Core SaaS and managed services ARR grew 24%, while total security-related revenues increased 10% to approximately $1.3 billion.

F5's Operating Margins Face Cost Pressures

Non-GAAP gross margin contracted 30 basis points year over year to 84%. Non-GAAP operating margin declined 330 basis points to 33.7%, reflecting higher operating expenses despite strong revenue growth.

Management attributed higher operating expenses partly to investments in sales capacity, AI security specialists and marketing. Strong year-end performance also increased commission and bonus expenses.

Non-GAAP operating income increased to $309 million from $299 million.

FFIV Maintains Solid Liquidity and Shareholder Returns

F5 generated $118 million in operating cash flow and $91 million in free cash flow during the quarter. Working capital investments, including inventory accumulation and supplier prepayments, affected cash generation as management secured components for future systems demand.

Cash and investments totaled $1.62 billion at quarter-end. The company repurchased $100 million of shares during the quarter, bringing fiscal 2026 repurchases to $600 million. Its board authorized an additional $1.5 billion for share repurchases, supplementing the $322 million remaining under the existing program.

F5 Issues Fiscal 2027 Growth Outlook

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, F5 expects revenues between $875 million and $895 million. Non-GAAP earnings are projected in the range of $4.25-$4.37 per share. Non-GAAP gross margin is expected between 81.5% and 82.5%.

For fiscal 2027, management projects revenue growth of 8-9% and non-GAAP earnings of $18.00-$18.30 per share. The company anticipates upper-single-digit systems growth, double-digit software growth and low-to-mid-single-digit services growth.

Non-GAAP gross margin is expected between 80.5% and 82.5%, suggesting higher component costs. Non-GAAP operating margin is projected at 33-35%. Management expects systems growth to be stronger in the first half, while software growth should accelerate in the second half of fiscal 2027 due to subscription renewal timing.

news.Title: Earnings Preview: Cirrus Logic (CRUS) Q2 Earnings Expected to Decline
news.Content:
Wall Street expects a year-over-year decline in earnings on lower revenues when Cirrus Logic (CRUS) reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. While this widely-known consensus outlook is important in gauging the company's earnings picture, a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on November 4, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This chipmaker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $2.44 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of -13.8%.

Revenues are expected to be $540.56 million, down 3.6% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 5.6% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Story Continues

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Cirrus Logic?

For Cirrus Logic, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.82%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #5.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Cirrus Logic will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Cirrus Logic would post earnings of $1.8 per share when it actually produced earnings of $1.84, delivering a surprise of +2.22%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Cirrus Logic doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

Expected Results of an Industry Player

Lattice Semiconductor (LSCC), another stock in the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, is expected to report earnings per share of $0.55 for the quarter ended September 2026. This estimate points to a year-over-year change of +96.4%. Revenues for the quarter are expected to be $255.13 million, up 91.3% from the year-ago quarter.

The consensus EPS estimate for Lattice has been revised 5.4% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. However, a lower Most Accurate Estimate has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.60%.

When combined with a Zacks Rank of #1 (Strong Buy), this Earnings ESP makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Lattice will beat the consensus EPS estimate. Over the last four quarters, the company surpassed consensus EPS estimates two times.

news.Title: 智原今年IP業務衝新高，明年12奈米加入再向上
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-28 09:33:29 黃立安 發佈

ASIC設計服務暨矽智財(IP)商智原(3035)總經理王國雍表示，受惠晶圓代工夥伴產能利用率維持高檔，以及IP授權與權利金收入成長，今年第四季IP營收有望挑戰單季新高，全年亦將創歷史新高。展望明(2027)年，隨晶圓代工夥伴持續擴產及調漲價格，權利金收入可望再創高，加上Intel與聯電(2303)合作的12奈米IP平台啟動開發，逐步挹注相關收入，對明年IP成長充滿信心。

王國雍指出，智原過去投入約3至4年時間，完成14奈米IP平台建置，目前相關IP協定及技術架構已逐步完善，且平台具備可重複使用的特性，不僅能支援既有ASIC設計業務，也有助縮短後續製程節點的開發時程，提升研發效率及成本競爭力。

下一階段布局以12奈米IP作為重點發展方向。王國雍表示，由於12奈米與14奈米製程具有高度相似性，可運用既有14奈米平台累積的技術及IP資產，加速12奈米IP開發，並配合12奈米製程平台，擴大相關業務布局，預期隨12奈米IP逐步開發完成，相關收入將陸續增加。

王國雍進一步指出，智原在IP開發上採取雙軌策略，一方面針對具市場規模的製程節點建立完整IP平台，另一方面則依客戶需求及投資報酬率(ROI)，選擇性投入更先進製程的IP開發，包括配合ASIC設計客戶、晶圓代工夥伴及自有Edge AI專案需求，以確保研發資源投入能帶來實際商業效益。

展望明年，王國雍表示，隨晶圓代工夥伴持續擴充產能、產能利用率維持高檔，加上晶圓代工價格調漲，預期權利金收入將進一步提升並再創新高；同時，12奈米IP平台開始投入開發，相關IP收入可望逐步貢獻，對2027年整體IP營收持續成長持正向看法。

news.Title: Rosenblatt names top semiconductor picks amid data-center strength
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Rosenblatt Securities has named AMD as its top semiconductor pick heading into earnings season, citing strengthening data-center fundamentals and broadening demand despite recent share price declines across the sector.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The semiconductor group with significant data-center revenue exposure has seen share prices decline approximately 25% on average over the past month, according to Rosenblatt Securities. However, the firm notes that data-center fundamentals continue to strengthen, with supporting evidence including strong earnings reports from Penguin Solutions, Micron, TSMC, and Texas Instruments, along with Supermicro's positive preannouncement.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Rosenblatt Securities' top pick is supported by several growth catalysts. TSMC's 2nm capacity is expected to double in 2027, which will support the ramp of AMD's Venice server CPU family. The firm views Venice as the market's highest-performing server CPU, featuring 16 memory channels compared to 12 in the prior generation. AMD CEO Lisa Su recently increased the projected 2030 server CPU total addressable market to $220 billion from $120 billion.

Meta's Muse and other emerging personal AI agents are driving server CPU demand, according to the firm. Rosenblatt notes that strong CPU demand and greater memory capacity create favorable conditions for the company. The firm's primary concern for data-center growth in 2027 and beyond is supply-chain capacity rather than demand weakness. Lam Research cited near-term supply constraints, while Texas Instruments highlighted extended lead times for back-end equipment.

However, Rosenblatt characterizes these as tactical challenges that the industry can address, rather than evidence of severe product shortages or weakening demand. The firm favors companies positioned to expand capacity and capture that demand.

news.Title: SCI Stock Surges More Than 111% in 6 Months: Can the Momentum Continue?
news.Content:
SCI Engineered Materials, Inc. 's SCIA investors have been gaining from the stock over the past few months. Shares of the Columbus, OH-based global supplier and manufacturer of advanced materials for Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) thin-film applications surged 111.3% in the past six months against the industry's 11.2% decline. It has also outperformed the sector and the S&P 500's gains of 6.6% and 6.4%, respectively, in the same time frame.

Two major developments of SCIA in recent months include the installation of a Plasma Spheroidization System or PSS (in August) and the announcement of its promising second-quarter 2026 results (in July).

In the second quarter, SCI reported record revenues and strong earnings growth, supported by higher raw material input costs, favorable product mix and increased volume. Higher revenues boosted gross profit, operating income and net income. However, gross margin contracted due to elevated raw material costs and product mix.

Management highlighted improving demand, new customer additions and growing traction in key markets. SCIA also expanded its workforce and ordered manufacturing equipment to support future growth, while interest in its specialized services continued to increase.

SCIA's Six-Month Price Comparison

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Over the past six months, the stock's performance has remained strong, outperforming its peers like Marvell Technology, Inc. MRVL and Cirrus Logic, Inc. CRUS. Marvell Technology and Cirrus Logic's shares have gained 52.6% and lost 30.5%, respectively, in the same time frame.

Despite risks related to significant customer concentration, fluctuating raw material costs and tariff uncertainties, SCI's favorable share price movement reflects positive investor sentiment.

SCIA primarily serves the photonics industry, supplying advanced materials for PVD thin-film applications. Its target markets include aerospace, automotive, defense, glass, optical coatings and solar. SCI collaborates with end users and original equipment manufacturers to develop customized material solutions.

SCIA's Growth Opportunities

SCI's expanding order backlog reflects improving business activity and provides greater visibility into potential future revenues. The backlog increased both sequentially and year over year at the end of the second quarter, indicating a stronger pipeline of customer orders. This development could support production planning and help sustain business activity as pending orders are fulfilled. Continued execution of these orders remains important for maintaining growth momentum.

Story Continues

SCI's installation of a PSS in August expanded its advanced materials manufacturing capabilities. The equipment enables the production of high-purity spherical powders suitable for additive manufacturing, including those derived from high-value precious metals. These capabilities could create opportunities in aeronautical, defense and biomedical applications, where material quality and performance are critical. Planned targeted marketing initiatives may help SCIA establish a stronger presence in these specialized markets.

SCI's toll manufacturing business offers additional opportunities beyond conventional material sales. Its capabilities include diffusion bonding, indium bonding, powder processing and vacuum hot pressing, addressing customers' specialized production requirements. Revenue from toll manufacturing and related services improved in the previous fiscal year, alongside growing demand for engineering-related projects. These customized offerings could deepen customer relationships and support additional business opportunities.

SCI's Financial Strength

SCI's operating cash flow strengthened during the first half of the year, supported by improved profitability and higher customer deposits. Cash reserves and working capital also increased from the previous year-end, reinforcing its liquidity position. These resources provide flexibility to meet operational requirements, fund equipment investments and pursue growth initiatives. The availability of an undrawn credit facility further supports its financial flexibility without immediately increasing borrowing obligations.

SCIA's ongoing share repurchase program reflects its commitment to shareholder-focused capital allocation. The company continued purchasing common shares during the first half of the year, reducing its share count and supporting earnings per share. Continued repurchases, subject to management discretion and business requirements, could further benefit per-share financial metrics.

Challenges Ahead of SCIA

SCI relies heavily on a limited number of major customers, exposing revenues to potential order reductions, delays or cancellations. The absence of minimum purchase commitments further heightens uncertainty regarding future sales visibility and business stability. SCIA's gross margins remain vulnerable to elevated raw material costs and unfavorable product mix. Its ability to protect profitability depends partly on passing higher input costs to customers without adversely affecting demand or competitive positioning.

SCI Stock's Valuation

SCI's trailing 12-month EV/Sales of 1.2X is lower than the industry's average of 13.3X but is higher than its five-year median of 0.6X.

Marvell Technology and Cirrus Logic's trailing 12-month EV/Sales currently stand at 21.8X and 2.3X, respectively.

Our Final Take on SCIA

SCI's impressive stock rally reflects strengthening business fundamentals and expanding growth opportunities. Its improving order pipeline, broader manufacturing capabilities and healthy financial position provide a supportive backdrop for continued business growth. However, customer concentration and cost-related pressures remain important considerations that could influence future performance.

From a valuation perspective, SCIA appears relatively inexpensive compared with the broader industry, suggesting potential room for further appreciation. However, its premium to historical valuation levels indicates that investors are already assigning greater value to its improving business prospects. This raises expectations for future performance and leaves less room for operational disappointments.

Overall, SCIA's positive momentum could continue if the company sustains operational improvements and capitalizes on emerging opportunities. Existing shareholders may consider maintaining their positions, while prospective investors may consider waiting for a more attractive entry point, given the sharp rally and valuation premium relative to historical levels.

news.Title: Investors Heavily Search Texas Instruments Incorporated (TXN): Here is What You Need to Know

Shares of this chipmaker have returned +7.1% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -0.8% change. Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Texas Instruments is expected to post earnings of $2.53 per share, indicating a change of +99.2% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +19.6% over the last 30 days.

The consensus earnings estimate of $8.85 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +62.4%. This estimate has changed +5.1% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $11.03 indicates a change of +24.7% from what Texas Instruments is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +12.1%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) for Texas Instruments.

Revenue Growth Forecast

While earnings growth is arguably the most superior indicator of a company's financial health, nothing happens as such if a business isn't able to grow its revenues. After all, it's nearly impossible for a company to increase its earnings for an extended period without increasing its revenues. So, it's important to know a company's potential revenue growth.

In the case of Texas Instruments, the consensus sales estimate of $6.09 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +37.7%. The $22.26 billion and $25.62 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +25.9% and +15.1%, respectively.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $5.93 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +2.17%. The EPS surprise was +9.17%.

Over the last four quarters, Texas Instruments surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times. The company topped consensus revenue estimates three times over this period.

Valuation

No investment decision can be efficient without considering a stock's valuation. Whether a stock's current price rightly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects is an essential determinant of its future price performance.

While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.

The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

news.Content:
How much a stock's price changes over time is important for most investors, since price performance can both impact your investment portfolio and help you compare investment results across sectors and industries.

The fear of missing out, or FOMO, also plays a factor in investing, especially with particular tech giants, as well as popular consumer-facing stocks.

What if you'd invested in Texas Instruments (TXN) ten years ago? It may not have been easy to hold on to TXN for all that time, but if you did, how much would your investment be worth today?

Texas Instruments' Business In-Depth

With that in mind, let's take a look at Texas Instruments' main business drivers.

Headquartered in Dallas, TX, Texas Instruments Incorporated is an original equipment manufacturer of analog, mixed-signal and digital signal processing (DSP) integrated circuits.

Texas Instruments has manufacturing and design facilities, including wafer fabrication and assembly/test operations in North America, Asia and Europe.

Management's strategy has been to build assets that would be fully utilized through their lifetimes and outsource any excess demand in peak situations to outside foundries.

In 2025, Texas Instruments generated total revenues of $17.68 billion, up 13% from 2024. The company has two reporting financial segments, Analog and Embedded Processing. It reports the results of its remaining business activities in Other.

Analog segment revenues grew 15% to $14.01 billion and accounted for approximately 79% of total revenues in 2025. Analog products have been categorized into two categories, Power and Signal Chain. Power products manage and distribute electricity, while Signal Chain products sense, condition and convert real-world signals.

Revenues from the Embedded Processing segment rose 6% to $2.70 billion and contributed approximately 15% to 2025 total revenues. This segment includes microcontrollers, processors, wireless connectivity and radar products.

The Other business generated $979 million in revenues and accounted for approximately 6% of 2025 total sales. The segment includes smaller product lines, such as DLP products, calculators and certain application-specific integrated circuits. Revenues from this segment increased 3% in 2025.

The company's products are sold in industrial, personal electronics, automotive, data center and communications equipment markets. In 2025, industrial and automotive each represented 33% of revenue. Personal electronics accounted for 21%, data center 9% and communications equipment 3%. Calculators represented about 1% of revenue.

Texas Instruments has more than 80,000 products and over 100,000 customers. In 2025, more than 80% of revenue was generated through direct sales channels.

Story Continues

Bottom Line

Anyone can invest, but building a successful investment portfolio requires research, patience, and a little bit of risk. So, if you had invested in Texas Instruments, ten years ago, you're likely feeling pretty good about your investment today.

According to our calculations, a $1000 investment made in October 2016 would be worth $4,157.30, or a gain of 315.73%, as of October 27, 2026, and this return excludes dividends but includes price increases.

Compare this to the S&P 500's rally of 258.82% and gold's return of 203.96% over the same time frame.

Analysts are anticipating more upside for TXN.

Texas Instruments is benefiting from a broad recovery in industrial and automotive demand and sustained data center expansion. Its analog and embedded portfolios serve diverse, long-lived applications. Internal manufacturing and growing capacity strengthen supply reliability while supporting margin recovery as utilization rises. Rising cash generation provides greater room for dividends and long-term investment. The planned Silicon Labs acquisition could extend its wireless connectivity reach. Management's outlook points to continued demand across its core markets. Semiconductor cyclicality, pricing competition, trade exposure and debt remain risks. Equipment delivery constraints could also slow capacity additions. Nonetheless, improving factory economics and a wider range of growth opportunities support an Outperform view.

The stock is up 7.12% over the past four weeks, and no earnings estimate has gone lower in the past two months, compared to 9 higher, for fiscal 2026. The consensus estimate has moved up as well.

news.Title: 智原Q4營收估季持平；明年三大產品線齊向上
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-27 16:42:18 黃立安 發佈

ASIC設計服務暨矽智財(IP)廠智原(3035)今(27)日舉行法說會，總經理王國雍表示，今(2026)年第四季IP業績可望續創高，NRE業務也將顯著成長，不過量產業務可能下滑，整體單季營收將較第三季的36.6億元約略持平，毛利率則回升至45%。2027年營收將成長兩位數，包括IP、NRE和量產三大產品線均可望同步向上。此外，近期先進製程成功接下美國客戶2奈米雲端AI應用專案，總金額高達數千萬美元，成為智原史上最大規模專案。

針對該2奈米專案，王國雍表示，此為首個2奈米環繞閘極(GAA)製程專案，原本客戶計劃採用4奈米製程，但考量到產品生命週期，決定改採2奈米製程，且專案總金額達數千萬美元，預計2027年上半年將有第一筆收入入帳，後續依進度認列，此案是智原史上最大金額的專案，將採用三星的晶圓代工，另外還與聯電(2303)及記憶體廠等夥伴合作。

王國雍指出，此項AI專案對公司深具指標性意義，並於四個面向均創下公司紀錄-設計製程、設計複雜度、NRE金額規模及高階封裝技術，同時此除證明客戶對公司設計能力的肯定及信賴，亦為後續先進製程及高階封裝接單及推廣建立了重要的指標性案例。

回顧第三季表現，智原在量產業務帶動下，單季營收達36.6億元，不僅優於原先預期，更逆勢季增11%、年增13%；毛利率42.5%，季減2.7個百分點、年增9.3個百分點；營業利益為2.1億元，季減21%，雖較第二季小幅回落，但受到營收規模擴大及毛利結構改善，年增達443%；營業利益率5.8%；稅後淨利2.8億元，季增41%，年增84%，EPS為1.07元。

智原2026年第三季營運創下多項紀錄，包括IP營收創歷史新高，量產及單季合併營收雙雙寫下歷年同期新高。

以產品別來看，IP營收4.5億元，季增4%，年增8%，創下歷史新高；NRE收入為3.1億元，季減31%，年減37%；量產營收則為第三季季主要成長動能，不僅MCU相關營收再創單季新高，ASIC量產在AI相關高階封裝專案出貨動能加速下，亦同步走揚，推升量產營收季增20%，年增25%，達29.1億元，創下歷年同期高點。

力成Q4及明年營運看正向；漲價效益續顯

news.Title: 智原第三季每股賺1.07元，成功搶下2奈米AI專案明年上半年開始入帳
news.Content:
【財訊快報／記者李純君報導】智原(3035)今日召開法說會，公布第三季成績單，單季本業部分，量產業務大增，業外收益也同時進補，帶動單季每股淨利1.07元，展望第四季，估營收與前季持平，IP持續成長創新高，NRE顯著成長，量產業務下滑，至於第四季毛利率估為45%。產線斬獲部分，獲得國際客戶開案，採用2奈米GAA製程，承接瞄準雲端AI應用之大型專案，預計2027年上半年會開始有收益。智原第三季受惠量產業務大幅成長，單季合併營收達36.64億元，季增10.6%、年增13.2%；營收中，IP營收4.48億元，季增3.5%、年增8.4%；NRE營收3.09億元，季減31.3%、年減37.1%；量產業務營收則達29.07億元，季增19.6%、年增24.7%，成為推升整體營收成長的主要動能。

獲利方面，智原第三季營業毛利15.57億元，季增3.9%、年增44.9%；毛利率42.5%，雖低於第二季的45.2%，但仍明顯高於去年同期的33.2%。第三季營業利益率為5.8%，低於第二季的8.2%，但優於去年同期的1.3%。但智原第三季業外收入達到2.66億元，季增138.8%、年增53.2%，主因業外轉投資評價利益挹注，挹注第三季本期淨利增至3.69億元，季增29.2%、年增124.1%。第三季歸屬母公司業主稅後淨利為2.79億元，季增40.8%、年增83.8%，單季每股淨利1.07元，。

展望第四季，公司自估，營收與第三季相比，大致約持平，毛利率估為45%。產線方面，IP持續成長創新高，NRE顯著成長，量產業務下滑。至於在產品線的斬獲部分，智原總經理王國雍透露，藉由和聯電(2303)、三星，以及記憶體廠等廠商的合作，公司已經獲得總金額數千萬美元、美系業者的2奈米AI雲端專案訂單。而整體2027年，智原看法樂觀，營收會年增雙位數百分比，三大產線都會年增。

news.Title: 智原攜手三星、聯電　搶下美國2奈米雲端AI專案訂單
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中新竹2026年10月27日電）特殊應用晶片廠智原 (3035) 總經理王國雍今天表示，透過與三星（Samsung）、聯電 (2303) 和記憶體廠等夥伴合作，成功搶下美國廠商2奈米雲端人工智慧（AI）專案訂單，總金額高達數千萬美元，是智原史上最大規模專案。

智原今天召開線上法人說明會，王國雍說，智原客戶委託設計（NRE）業務在先進製程有新斬獲，成功搶下2奈米環繞閘極（GAA）製程雲端AI專案訂單，這對智原意義重大，是最先進的製程，也是第1個2奈米GAA製程專案，複雜度也最高。

王國雍表示，原本客戶計劃採用4奈米製程，基於延長產品生命週期考量，決定改採2奈米製程；這專案總金額達數千萬美元，預計2027年上半年將有第1筆收入入帳，後續依進度認列，是智原史上最大金額的專案。

王國雍說，智原具備設計以及統籌協調能力，是能夠搶下2奈米專案的關鍵，此案將採用三星的晶圓代工，另外還與聯電及記憶體廠等夥伴合作。

智原第3季受惠量產業務優於預期，加上矽智財（IP）業績創下歷史新高，整體第3季營收攀高至新台幣36.64億元，季增10.6%，為歷年同期新高。

受產品組合變化影響，低毛利的量產業務比重攀升，智原第3季毛利率42.5%，較第2季下滑2.7個百分點，營業利益2.14億元，季減20.8%，受惠業外轉投資評價利益挹注，智原第3季歸屬母公司淨利2.79億元，季增40.8%，每股純益1.07元。

展望未來，智原預期，第4季IP業績可望持續成長創高，NRE業務將顯著成長，量產業務可能下滑，整體第4季營收將較第3季持平，毛利率約45%。

王國雍表示，2027年營收將成長2位數，包括IP、NRE和量產3大產品線2027年營收可望同步成長。

news.Content:

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, on Monday disclosed rapid revenue growth alongside steep losses in its IPO filing, highlighting both the commercial potential of generative AI and the substantial costs of developing advanced models.
